"Homage to all the worthy and holy ones, the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

Namo to Ājñātakauṇḍinya; namo to Mahākāśyapa; namo to Uruvilvākāśyapa; namo to Gayākāśyapa; namo to Nadīkāśyapa; namo to Śāriputra; namo to Mahāmaudgalyāyana; namo to Mahākātyāyana; namo to Aniruddha; namo to MahāKapphiṇa. I take refuge in these and other such great Arhats who are well-known to the world."
"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next perform repentance. Disciples!

Having already repented of the obstacle of afflictions and having already repented of the obstacle of karma, we shall now proceed to lay bare and repent of the remaining obstacle of retribution in due order."

"When the retribution of karma arrives, there is no escape in the void, nor in the midst of the ocean, nor by entering between mountain rocks; there is no other place where one may avoid receiving it. Only through the power of repentance can it be extinguished."
How is this known to be so?

When Śakra Devānām-indra manifested the five signs of decline, his heart was overcome with fear, and by taking refuge with sincere devotion in the Triple Gem, the signs of death were immediately extinguished and his celestial lifespan was extended.
Innumerable instances such as these are clarified in the scriptural teachings; therefore, we know that repentance truly can extinguish calamity.

However, if ordinary persons do not encounter the guidance of virtuous friends, there is no evil they will not commit, which causes the terrifying visions of hell to appear before them at the final moment when their lives are about to end.
At that moment, remorse and fear will come upon him all at once. Having failed to cultivate goodness beforehand, he now regrets it when facing his end; what can such subsequent regret avail?

Calamities and misfortunes await him in another realm, prepared in advance; he must go alone to a distant place, where he enters first into a great cauldron, his body and mind shattered and his spirit in agony.
At such a time, how could one possibly seek even a single prostration or a single confession?

You all must not rely on your youth, wealth, treasures, or power to indulge in indolence, laziness, negligence, and self-indulgence. When the suffering of death arrives, it makes no distinction between old and young; whether poor or rich, noble or lowly, all are utterly extinguished. It comes suddenly and unexpectedly, leaving no one to know it has arrived.
Life is impermanent, like the morning dew; though the outgoing breath may enter, the incoming breath is difficult to preserve. How can one fail to repent for this?
"Furthermore, once the five divine messengers have arrived and the executioner of impermanence has suddenly come, even those in the prime of youth and vigor cannot escape."
At that time, what concern do the magnificent halls and deep chambers have for human affairs?

How could high carriages and great horses follow one of their own accord? Wives, children, and kinsmen are no longer one's kin; the ornaments of the seven treasures become merely the playthings of others.

Speaking from this perspective, all worldly retributions are like illusions and transformations; though the heavens above are pleasant, they ultimately return to decay, and when one's lifespan is exhausted, the soul falls into the three miserable realms.
Therefore, the Buddha said to Subhadra:

"Your teacher Udraka Rāmaputra possessed sharp faculties and great intelligence, and was able to subdue his afflictions; yet when his life ended at the Peak of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-perception, he returned to take birth as a flying weasel within the realm of animals. How much more so, then, for others?"

Thus we know that until one has realized the fruits of sainthood, one must continue to transmigrate and undergo all the miserable realms; if one is not careful, one may suddenly find oneself caught up in such matters one day, leaving no time for regret.

Suppose, for instance, one is now brought before the official gate on charges of a crime; this is already a minor suffering, yet the spirit is filled with terror and the kinsfolk are struck with fear, seeking salvation by every possible means. Compared to this, the manifold sufferings of the hells are hundreds of thousands of millions of times greater and cannot even be illustrated by analogy. All of you have, together, accumulated sins over successive kalpas as vast as Mount Sumeru.
How can you hear this and remain composed, neither fearing, nor being startled, nor being terrified?
To cause these spirits to once again be afflicted by such suffering is truly a matter of great pity. Therefore, disciples!
With this singular sincerity and a devoted heart, I take refuge in the Buddha:

Namo to the Buddha Tamer of Men in the East; Namo to the Buddha Vajragarbha in the South; Namo to the Buddha Lamp of the Dharma-realm in the West; Namo to the Buddha Boundless Eye in the North; Namo to the Buddha Sorrowless Virtue in the Southeast; Namo to the Buddha Destroyer of All Fears in the Southwest; Namo to the Buddha Valiant Subduer in the Northwest; Namo to the Buddha Great Power Radiance in the Northeast; Namo to the Buddha Joyful Path in the Nadir; Namo to the Buddha Supreme Fragrance King in the Zenith. I take refuge in all such Triple Gems throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of empty space.

“Disciples! From time immemorial until this very day, there have been all manner of karmic obstructions to retribution. Among these, the most grave is first and foremost the Avīci Hell, as clarified in the sutras; I shall now briefly describe its characteristics.”

This hell is surrounded on all sides by seven layers of iron walls, further covered above by seven layers of iron nets; below, there are seven layers of sword-forests and immeasurable fierce fires, extending eighty-four thousand yojanas in length and breadth.

The bodies of the sinners fill the entire space; through the causal conditions of their sinful karma, they do not obstruct one another. The upper flames penetrate downward and the lower flames penetrate upward; east, west, south, and north are completely permeated and intermingled. Just as when fish are placed in a cauldron and their fat and grease are entirely consumed, so too is the suffering of the sinners within this place.
"At the four gates of that city are four great bronze dogs; their bodies are forty *yojanas* in length and breadth, with fangs and claws as sharp as razors and eyes like flashes of lightning.

Furthermore, there are immeasurable birds with iron beaks that soar and wheel about, pecking at the flesh of the sinners. The ox-headed hell-wardens have forms like *rākṣasas*, each possessing nine tails, and their tails are like iron forks."

Furthermore, it has eight heads, each with eighteen horns and sixty-four eyes; from every single eye, glowing iron balls burst forth, burning the flesh of the sinners. Moreover, whenever it bellows in a fit of rage and fury, its voice is like a thunderclap.

Furthermore, immeasurable natural blades and wheels descend from the air, entering through the crowns of the sinners' heads and exiting through their feet; thus, the pain of these sinners penetrates to the very marrow of their bones, cutting through their livers and hearts with agonizing intensity.
Thus, for immeasurable years, they have endured various sufferings and afflictions, unable to seek birth and unable to seek death.
For such retributions as these, we today all prostrate ourselves with shame and remorse, confessing them with a sincere heart.
"I repent for the retribution of my crimes that caused my body and head to be severed in the remaining hells of the Mountain of Blades and the Forest of Swords.
I repent for the retribution of my crimes that caused me to be burned and boiled in the Hell of Cauldrons and the Hell of Stoves and Charcoal."
I repent for the retribution of my sins that causes the burning hells of the iron bed and copper pillar;
I repent for the retribution of my sins that causes the crushing hells of the wheel of blades and the flaming chariot;
I repent for the retribution of my sins that causes the hells of the ploughed tongue and the ox-drawn harrow, where agonizing pain prevails.
I repent for the retribution of my sins in the Iron Ball and Molten Copper-Quaffing Hell, where my five internal organs were consumed and rotted away.
I repent for the retribution of my sins in the Iron Pestle and Iron Mill Hell, where my flesh and bones were ground into dust.
I repent for the retribution of my sins that led to the Black Rope and Iron Net Hells, where my limbs and joints were severed and torn apart.
I repent for the retribution of my sins that led to the Ash River and Boiling Excrement Hells, where I suffered from distress and suffocation.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being naked and frozen in the Salt Water and Cold Ice Hells, where the skin is split and cracked open.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being mutually harmed and killed in the Hells of Tigers, Wolves, Hawks, and Dogs.
"I repent for the karmic retribution of being struck, seized, hacked, and pierced in the Hell of the Parting of Swords;
I repent for the karmic retribution of being roasted on spits in the Hell of the Fire Pit."
I repent for the retribution of my sins in the Hell of Two Rocks Grinding Together, where my physical form was shattered to pieces.
I repent for the retribution of my sins in the Hell of Black-Eared Assemblage, where I was dismembered and torn apart.
Repentance for the retribution of being hacked and minced in the Dark Flesh Mountain Hell.
Repentance for the retribution of having one's body sawn apart and nailed down in the Hell of the Sawing Body.
Repentance for the retribution of being butchered and sliced while suspended upside down with iron clubs in the Hell of the Iron Clubs.
In the Avīci Hell of Intense Heat and Wailing, we repent for the retribution of our grievances and transgressions.
Between the Great and Small Iron Ring Mountains, where the long night is dark and one knows not the three luminaries, we repent for the retribution of our sins.

"In the Āpāpa hell, the Āśāśa hell, the Aṭaṭa hell, the Alala hell, and so forth—within all these eight cold and eight hot hells, each individual hell further has eighty-four thousand subsidiary hells as its retinue."

Within these realms of sin and suffering, there are the agonies of being roasted and boiled, the flaying of skin and the hacking away of flesh, the sawing of bones and the pounding of marrow, and the extraction of entrails and lungs—immeasurable sufferings that are neither fit to be heard nor fit to be described.

Those who are here within these realms today may have been our parents throughout countless lifetimes since beginningless time, or all manner of our kinsmen; after we pass away, we too may fall into such hells as these.

Today, having cleansed my heart with utmost sincerity, I prostrate myself with my forehead touching the ground before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas throughout the great earth, entreating their compassion and repenting so that all these karmic obstacles may be utterly extinguished.

"May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession of retributions such as those of the hells, pray that in every birth and every life, the compassion of all Buddhas shall rescue sentient beings from suffering; may they then shatter the iron city of Avīci, so that it becomes entirely like a Pure Land where even the name of the evil realms no longer exists."

All other instruments of suffering in the hells were transformed into conditions of happiness; the mountains of knives and trees of swords became jeweled couches, and the boiling cauldrons and burning coals were transformed into lotuses where beings were born. The ox-headed hell-wardens abandoned their cruelty and, free from all evil intent, gave rise to compassion for all.

The sentient beings in the hells, having attained liberation from the fruits of suffering and no longer creating further causes, experience equal peace and bliss as if in the third dhyāna; simultaneously, they all give rise to the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment.

In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Concerning Retribution for Śramaṇas*, titled "The Jewel-Attainment of the Lotus," Bodhiruci (Bǎodá) shortly thereafter entered the Hell of Drinking Molten Metal (Yǐnhuǒzhū Dìyù).
Why is it called the Hell of Drinking Molten Metal?

That hell is three hundred yojanas in length and breadth; its iron walls encircle it on all sides as smoke and fire rise together. Upon the ground are cauldrons filled with boiling iron dregs in a turbulent mass, and at their edges stand horse-headed rākṣasas holding iron ladles with which they scoop up the iron dregs.

Within the eastern gate were eight thousand śramaṇas, wailing and weeping with their body hairs burning like fire and smoke and flames rising together; as they walked, these sinful bhikṣus repeatedly fell and stumbled at every step.

The horse-headed rākṣasa grasps a three-pronged iron trident and thrusts it toward the chest, so that it emerges from the back; the prongs of the trident are ablaze, piercing through both sides. The yakṣa jailer grasps an iron hook and strikes the jaw, so that it emerges from the mouth.
At that time, the eyes and mouth of the sinner gape open.

Then, the hell-warden takes an iron ladle filled with glowing iron pellets and pours them into the sinner’s mouth; they emerge from all six sense organs, emitting smoke and flames that blaze intensely, while the pores of his body are likewise set ablaze.

For one day and one night, they undergo myriad forms of suffering, undergoing a thousand deaths and a thousand births, ten thousand deaths and ten thousand births. Even if they should obtain a human body, it will be incomplete; being deaf, blind, or mute, they shall not hear the name of the Buddha, nor shall they behold even a thousand Buddhas appearing in the world.
The Bodhisattva Ratnabhadra asked the horse-headed rākṣasa,
"What karma did these śramaṇas commit to undergo such punishment?
"These śramaṇas have received the pure precepts of the Buddha yet do not maintain them with purity; they consume the faithful offerings of others while failing to observe the fast themselves.
They eat at night and even prepare their own food with their own hands, taking it for themselves without any sense of shame or remorse."
"By these causes and conditions, one undergoes such retribution.
Upon hearing this, Bodhidharma wept with sorrow and departed.

"Namo to Gavāmpati; namo to Revata; namo to Piṅgalavatsa; namo to Bakula; namo to Mahākauṣṭhila; namo to Nanda; namo to Sundarananda; namo to Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra; namo to Subhūti; namo to Cūdapanthaka. I take refuge in these and all other great Arhats who are well-known to the world."
"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we now proceed to repentance. Disciples!
Having already repented for the retributions of the hells, we shall now, in turn, repent for the retributions of the three evil realms."
In the Sūtra, the Buddha said:
"The person of great desire suffers much affliction because they seek many profits;
the person who is content, even though lying upon the bare ground, still considers it happiness."
"Those who lack contentment find no satisfaction even while dwelling in heaven.

Yet worldly people, when suddenly confronted by urgent calamities, are able to relinquish their wealth without regard for its quantity; they fail to realize that this body stands upon the edge of the deep pits of the three miserable realms, and that with but a single breath not returned, it will surely fall.

Suddenly, a spiritual friend instructs one to cultivate merit and to prepare the provisions for wholesome dharmas in the future; yet, clinging to this stingy mind, one refuses to act upon the principle [of practice]. Indeed, such a person is utterly foolish and deluded.
Why is this so? In the sutras, the Buddha said:
"At the time of birth, one does not bring a single coin; at the time of death, one likewise does not take a single coin with one."

Toiling with a suffering body and accumulating [wealth] for it brings only anxiety and distress; it benefits oneself not at all but serves only the interests of others. With no goodness to rely upon and no virtue to depend on, one’s life comes to an end and one falls into the various evil realms.
"Therefore, disciples! Today, with utmost sincerity, bowing our heads in prostration and with earnest, devoted hearts, we take refuge in the Buddha.

Homage to the Buddha Great Radiance in the East; Homage to the Buddha Dwelling in Space in the South; Homage to the Buddha Vajra-Stride in the West; Homage to the Buddha Boundless Power in the North; Homage to the Buddha Boundless King in the Southeast; Homage to the Buddha Destroyer of All Enemies in the Southwest; Homage to the Buddha Stainless Light in the Northwest; Homage to the Buddha Golden Light-Sound in the Northeast; Homage to the Buddha Lion’s Play in the Nadir; Homage to the Buddha Moon Banner King in the Zenith. We take refuge in all such Triple Gems throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the realm of empty space."
"Disciples! Today we further repent for the retribution of our sins in the realm of animals, where there is no consciousness or knowledge;
we repent for the retribution of our sins in the realm of animals, such as carrying heavy loads and pulling plows to repay the debts of past lives."
I repent for the karmic retribution of being unable to attain self-mastery within the realm of animals, being cut, pierced, slaughtered, and dismembered by others;
I repent for the karmic retribution of having no feet, two feet, four feet, or many feet within the realm of animals;
I repent for the karmic retribution of having my body’s hair, feathers, scales, or shells devoured by various small insects within the realm of animals.
We repent for such immeasurable and boundless retributions for sins within the realm of animals; today, with utmost sincerity, we take refuge and repent.
Today, we further repent for the karmic retribution of long-term hunger within the realm of hungry ghosts;
we repent for the karmic retribution of never having heard the names of even water or gruel for hundreds of thousands of myriads of years within the realm of hungry ghosts;
and we repent for the karmic retribution of consuming pus, blood, excrement, and filth within the realm of hungry ghosts.
I repent for the karmic retribution of having all my limbs and joints ablaze with fire whenever I moved my body while in the realm of hungry ghosts;
I repent for the karmic retribution of having a vast belly and a narrow throat while in the realm of hungry ghosts.
We repent for such immeasurable and boundless retributions of suffering within the realm of hungry ghosts; therefore, today we prostrate with utmost sincerity, taking refuge and repenting.
Today, I further repent for the karmic retribution of flattery, deceit, and false claims within the realms of all ghosts, spirits, and asuras;
I repent for the karmic retribution of carrying sand and bearing stones, filling rivers and blocking seas, within the realm of ghosts and spirits;
and I repent for the karmic retribution of being born with such ugliness among the various evil ghosts and spirits—such as *piśācas*, *kumbhāṇḍas*, and others—who devour flesh and blood raw.

I repent of all such immeasurable and boundless retributions for sins within the realm of ghosts and spirits; today, with my head bowed to the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas of the great earth, I seek their compassion and repent so that all may be utterly extinguished.

"May we disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this repentance for the retribution of animal births, vow that in every life and birth we shall extinguish the defilement of ignorance, recognize our own karmic conditions, possess the clear illumination of wisdom, and sever the body of the evil realms."

By the merit produced through this repentance for the retribution of hungry ghosts and others, may we, in life after life, forever be free from the suffering of stinginess, greed, hunger, and thirst, and always partake of the nectar-like flavor of liberation.

I vow that by the merit produced through this repentance for the retributions of ghosts, spirits, and asuras, may I, in life after life, be upright and sincere without guile; may I be free from the causes of wrong livelihood and eliminate the fruits of ugliness, thereby bringing benefit and fortune to humans and devas.

May we, the disciples, from this day forth until we reach the site of enlightenment, certainly not receive the retribution of the four evil realms; except only when, out of great compassion for the sake of sentient beings, we dwell therein through the power of our vows without weariness.

In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Concerning Retribution for Śramaṇas*, titled "The Jewel-Attainer," Boread (Bao-da) shortly thereafter entered another hell, named the Hell of Flying Blades.

That hell is fifteen *yojanas* in length and breadth, surrounded on all sides by iron walls and covered above by an iron lattice. At the four corners of the city, fierce winds of fire blow against iron mountains; as these mountains grind against one another, they form sharp blades. These blades have two edges like the points of awls; their whirring and clattering in the void is like the sound of thunder, and the clashing of blade against blade is like a crash of lightning. Descending from the sky, they pierce the heads of the offenders, entering at the head and exiting beneath the feet, or entering at the back and exiting at the chest. They emerge from the left and enter from the right, with smoke and flames blazing together. For one day and one night, they undergo myriad forms of suffering, dying and being reborn a thousand times, ten thousand times. Even if they should obtain a human body, they will be born with malignant sores covering their entire bodies.
"What kind of conduct did these śramaṇas perform to undergo such suffering?

"These śramaṇas have received the pure precepts of the Buddha yet do not maintain them with purity; their minds lack compassion as they drink alcohol and eat meat, claiming there is no retribution for such acts. The sin of eating meat is logically unforgivable, and it is because of these causes and conditions that they undergo this punishment."
Upon hearing this, Bodhisattva Baoda wept with grief and departed.

"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next proceed to repentance.

'Disciples! Having already repented for the retributions of the three miserable realms and so forth, we shall now, in turn, prostrate ourselves with earnest sincerity to repent for the remaining retributions within the human and celestial realms.'"

Together we have received this lifespan of Jambudvīpa; though it is said to be a full hundred years, those who complete it are few indeed. Within that interval, those whose prime years end in premature death are immeasurable in number. There is only the constant pressure of manifold sufferings upon body and mind, such that grief, anxiety, fear, and dread never depart for even a moment.

All such instances arise because one's roots of goodness are feeble while evil karma is abundant, causing whatever one does in the present to be contrary to one's wishes; one should know that these are entirely the residual retributions of evil karma from the past.
Therefore, disciples! Today, with utmost sincerity, we take refuge in the Buddha: Homage to the Buddha Padmottara in the east.

"Disciples! From time immemorial until this very day, regarding all present and future karmic retributions among humans and devas—immeasurable residual consequences, lingering calamities, past karmic confrontations, chronic ailments, physical infirmities, and the retribution of offenses for the impairment of the six sense faculties—we now repent."
I repent for the retributive offenses of holding wrong views in the human borderlands and the three evil paths, as well as the eight difficulties;
I repent for the retributive offenses of frequent illness, emaciation, shortened lifespans, and untimely deaths among humans;
I repent for the retributive offenses of being unable to always maintain mutual protection and harmony with one's six types of kinsmen and relatives.
I repent for the karmic retribution of the suffering of separation from loved ones due to the death of human friends;
I repent for the karmic retribution of the suffering of grief, anxiety, and fear caused by encounters with human enemies;
I repent for the karmic retribution of alarm, terror, and dread caused by the perils of fire, water, bandits, and weapons in the human world.
I repent for the retribution of being solitary, distressed, wandering, and scattered abroad among humans, having lost my kingdom;
I repent for the retribution of being imprisoned, confined, shackled, and subjected to flogging and torture in human prisons;
I repent for the retribution of being entangled in public and private disputes among humans, mutually implicated and mutually slandered.
I repent for the retribution of my sins that cause chronic, malignant diseases in the human world which do not subside for years or months, leaving one bedridden and unable to rise or move;
I repent for the retribution of my sins that cause winter fevers, summer epidemics, virulent poisons, and contagious colds in the human world;
I repent for the retribution of my sins that cause the calamities of "thief-wind," swellings, distensions, and obstructions in the human world.
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans being sought out by various evil deities who watch for an opportunity to inflict calamity and misfortune;
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans being subjected to the strange anomalies caused by birds that shriek, the hundred monsters, flying corpses, and malevolent ghosts;
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans being harmed by tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, and all manner of evil beasts of land and water.
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans who bind themselves, pierce themselves, commit suicide, or harm themselves;
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans who grieve themselves, lament themselves, restrain themselves, become angry with themselves, or rejoice in themselves;
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans who throw themselves into pits, rush into fire, drown themselves, or fall from heights.
I repent for the karmic retribution of lacking dignity, virtue, and renown among humans;
I repent for the karmic retribution of being unable to satisfy my heart's desires regarding clothing and the necessities of life among humans;
I repent for the karmic retribution of encountering evil associates who create obstacles and hindrances whenever I travel, enter or exit, or engage in any activity among humans.

In this way, within the realms of humans and devas of the present and future, we repent for immeasurable calamities, untimely deaths, pestilences, misfortunes, afflictions, and karmic retributions. Disciples!
Today, with utmost sincerity, before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Assembly of Sages, I bare my liver and expose my heart to seek compassion and repent.
"May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this repentance, [attain...]".
May I, in birth after birth, be endowed with a perfect physical form, just like Rāhula;
may I always encounter the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and constantly hear the sublime Dharma; may my lifespan be equal to that of heaven and earth; may I not be afflicted by the hundred maladies;
may my six kin and relatives always receive mutual protection; and may enemies, bandits, and weapons be eternally removed from me, so that all things occur spontaneously.
Clothing chests and baskets were always full; bowls of fragrant food of a hundred flavors were constantly filled; prisons and places of confinement were transformed into heavenly paradises;
verbal disputes and mutual slanders became harmonious and reconciled; chronic illnesses were forever removed from body and mind;
pestilence, poisons, and various calamities were perpetually kept away from their heads; and malevolent spirits, *piśāca* demons, and even predatory birds [ceased to cause harm].
May all calamities and misfortunes— whether from tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, or various dangers of water and land— be eliminated without remainder.
Whether [the offenses] were committed through self-inflicted mutilation or through self-induced anger and joy,
may such transgressions be forever severed and separated from me from this moment until the attainment of Buddhahood.

"May we disciples not receive retribution in the various evil realms; may we instead give rise to great compassion to rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing them all to fulfill their natures and extensively transform all classes of beings so that they may together ascend to perfect enlightenment."
In the *Mahāyāna Padma-ratna-bodhi-praśna-pratyaya-śramaṇa-sūtra*, Bodhi entered the Hell of Flaming Arrows (Huǒjiàn dìyù) shortly thereafter.
Why is it called the Hell of Flaming Arrows?

That hell is ninety yojanas in length and breadth; it is surrounded on all sides by iron walls from which fierce flames blaze forth. The ground is strewn everywhere with iron spikes, and smoke and fire burn intensely as they come to scorch the offenders. From the four sides of that ground, putrid winds arise together, while from the void above, violent winds suddenly and swiftly blow against the iron mountains.

As those mountains rub against one another, they produce fire-arrows; as these fire-arrows grind together, the smoke and flames blaze intensely, and even the feathers on the shafts of the arrows catch fire. These arrows come to shoot at the sinners, entering through their heads and exiting from beneath their feet, or entering through their backs and exiting from their chests, piercing through their left and right sides until the wounds are ablaze with fire and emit thick smoke and flames.
The sinners wailed with unspeakable agony; for one day and one night they underwent immeasurable suffering, dying and being reborn a thousand times, ten thousand times.
"What sins did these śramaṇas commit that they come to receive this retribution?"

"These śramaṇas have received the pure precepts of the Buddha but do not maintain them with purity; they do not guard their dignified deportment according to the dharma, but instead hold bows and arrows in their hands, thereby losing the majestic demeanor of a Buddha."
As it is said in the Sūtra:

"In the past, there was a bhikṣu named Śāli who did not maintain proper decorum; because he took up a layperson's bow and arrow with his hand, he suffered its evil retribution for ten thousand generations."
"For this reason, you should know that a śramaṇa who does not guard his dignified demeanor falls into the three evil realms; this bhikṣu here is just like that.
Upon hearing this, Bodhiruci wept with grief and departed.

Homage to the *Māndārava-dārikā-ṣaḍvastu-vibhaṅga-sūtra*. "I pay homage to all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the ten directions.

homage to the Bodhisattva Vimalabuddhi. I take refuge in all such immeasurable and boundless great Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
"Homage to all the noble ones, the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Namo to the Venerable Aññākoṇḍañña; namo to the Venerable Sañjīva; namo to the Venerable Khema; namo to the Venerable Tissa Moggaliputta; namo to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāniputta; namo to the Venerable Upāli; namo to the Venerable Revata; namo to the Venerable Ānanda; namo to the Venerable Rāhula; namo to the Venerable Gavampati. I take refuge in such great arhats as these, who are renowned throughout the world."
"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next proceed to repentance.

Disciples! We respectfully invite the Buddhas of the ten directions, the twelve divisions of the scriptures, all worthy sages, the eight classes of devas and dragons, and all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, as well as the assembly present here, to bear witness.
Disciples! Since beginningless time, we have committed immeasurable and boundless transgressions; today, with a sincere heart, we reveal and repent of them, and take refuge in the Buddha.

“Homage to the Buddha Amitābha of the eastern direction; homage to the Buddha Sumeru of the southern direction; homage to the Buddha Vajrapadavyūha of the western direction; homage to the Buddha Bhadraśreṣṭha of the northern direction; homage to the Buddha Mahābhyudgatarocana of the southeastern direction; homage to the Buddha Ratnottama of the southwestern direction; homage to the Buddha Ekayāna of the northwestern direction; homage to the Buddha Mārajālasambhedaikavikrāmin of the northeastern direction; homage to the Buddha Akutobhayamati of the downward direction; homage to the Buddha Aparimitaguruvimalarāja of the upward direction. I take refuge in all such Triple Gems throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space in the ten directions.”
“Disciples! Now, for the sake of all sentient beings and for our own selves, we take refuge and repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions.

Throughout immeasurable kalpas, all sentient beings have failed to recognize the Buddhas and the kindness of their parents; they have not understood wholesome dharmas and have committed manifold evils. Relying on their own lineage and various wealth and treasures, they were heedless in their prime years and performed various evil deeds; their minds conceived what was unwholesome and their mouths committed evil karma, yet they failed to see the faults of what they created according to their own hearts.”

Ordinary worldlings act with folly and are shrouded in the darkness of ignorance; they associate with evil friends, their minds are disordered by afflictions, and due to the conditions of the five desires, anger arises in their hearts. Failing to know contentment, they commit various evils; associating with those who are not noble, they give rise to stinginess and envy.

Due to the causes and conditions of poverty, they act with deceit and craftiness, committing evil deeds; bound to others, they are constantly filled with fear. Lacking self-mastery, they create various evils; greed, hatred, and delusion agitate their minds. Pressed by thirsting craving, they commit various evils based on clothing, food, and female beauty. Tormented by the fever of various fetters and afflictions, their hearts become stained by attachment to other men. Or, regarding oxen, horses, donkeys, mules, sheep, and all manner of birds and beasts—every kind of diverse creature—they conceive thoughts of them as women. Not relying on the practice of the Buddha, they commit various evils.
The three types of karma accumulated through the actions of body, speech, and mind—such immeasurable and boundless transgressions as these, we now repent in their entirety. "Disciples!
From time immemorial until this very day, whether we have failed to show reverence to the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, such transgressions as these, we now repent in their entirety."
Or failing to show respect to pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas—such transgressions as these, I now repent in their entirety.

Because of ignorance, I slandered the True Dharma; I did not know how to revere my parents or elders; I was shrouded by folly and delusion, arrogant and heedless; and due to greed, hatred, and delusion, I committed various evils—all such transgressions as these, I now repent in their entirety.

I took pleasure in drinking alcohol without knowing moderation; I gave wine to the Saṃgha, to those who uphold the precepts, to bhikṣuṇīs, or to those who have extinguished their thoughts or are in meditative concentration. Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless; today, I direct my mind toward them and take refuge in repentance.

"Disciples! All the various evils committed since beginningless kalpas have, through these causes and conditions, given rise to great sorrow and suffering, poverty, destitution, anxiety, and fear. Terrified by evil karma, our minds are constantly timid and weak; in every place we dwell, there is not even a moment of joy. The World-Honored Ones of Great Compassion currently residing throughout the ten directions are able to remove all fears of sentient beings; we pray that you will accept our sincere repentance."

I now repent for all past evils; I sincerely confess and reveal all actions currently being committed; I dare not commit again those deeds not yet performed; and I dare not conceal those deeds already done. I now repent for the three types of physical karma, the four types of verbal karma, and the three types of mental karma. I now repent for all such perils as the hardships of birth and death, various forms of lust, and the difficulties of ignorance and affliction. I now repent for all these calamities.

The mind is difficult to keep from being flighty and restless; it is difficult to avoid evil friends; there are the perils of the three realms of existence and the perils of the three poisons; it is difficult to encounter freedom from such calamities, difficult to meet with a favorable time, difficult to cultivate merit, and difficult to meet a Buddha. All such difficulties as these, I now repent.

"Disciples! From beginningless kalpas until this present body, you have killed all members of the Triple Gem, teachers, parents, six types of relatives, spiritual friends, and sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm in numbers beyond calculation;
you have stolen all property belonging to the Triple Gem, teachers, parents, six types of relatives, spiritual friends, and sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm in numbers beyond calculation."

Toward all the Three Jewels, teachers and monks, parents, six classes of relatives, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, they give rise to unwholesome thoughts beyond measure.
"The number of instances of lying and deceiving all the Triple Gem, teachers, parents, the six kinds of relatives, spiritual friends, and sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm is unknowable;

the number of instances of frivolous speech used to mock and toy with all the Triple Gem, teachers, parents, the six kinds of relatives, spiritual friends, and sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm is unknowable;

the number of instances of harsh speech used to revile, slander, and disparage all the Triple Gem, teachers, parents, the six kinds of relatives, spiritual friends, and sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm is unknowable."

Through divisive speech, they cause strife and discord, destroying all the Three Jewels, teachers, monks, parents, the six classes of relatives, spiritual friends, and the sentient beings of the dharma realm, in numbers beyond calculation.

"Or they may break the five precepts, the eight precepts, the ten precepts, the ten wholesome precepts, the two hundred and fifty precepts, the five hundred precepts, the Bodhisattva’s threefold aggregate of precepts, the ten inexhaustible precepts, and even all precepts, as well as all rules of decorum and so forth."

The number of times I have committed such acts myself, taught others to do so, or rejoiced in their doing them is beyond calculation; these various transgressions are as numerous as the infinite atoms of dust throughout the great earths of the ten directions.

"Our committed transgressions are likewise infinite and incalculable: as space is infinite, our committed transgressions are also infinite; as skillful means are infinite, our committed transgressions are also infinite; as the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is infinite, our committed transgressions are also infinite; as the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is infinite, our committed transgressions are also infinite; as sentient beings are infinite, our acts of plundering and killing them are also infinite; as the Triple Gem is infinite, our acts of violating and damaging it are also infinite; and as the categories of precepts are infinite, our acts of breaking and transgressing them are also infinite."

Such offenses as these, reaching upward to those bodhisattvas and downward to the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, cannot be known by them; only a Buddha and a Buddha can know the extent of my transgressions.

Now, before the Triple Gem and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, I openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal anything; I only pray that the Triple Gem and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm throughout the ten directions will hear my confession.

“May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession, vow that in every birth and every life we shall forever abandon the womb. May our forms follow our vows to be reborn and attain the six supernormal powers, so as to rescue and gather all suffering beings; until the void and the dharma-realm are exhausted, may my vow remain thus.”

May all sentient beings in the hells and among the hungry ghosts—who are impoverished, beset by calamities, and oppressed by various sufferings and afflictions—be completely freed from such miseries as these.

"Furthermore, I pray that my disciples, by virtue of the merit accomplished through this confession, may depart from birth and death to reach the shore of Great Wisdom; may they turn the supreme wheel, which is subtle and pure, and may all their aspirations and requests be fully accomplished."

"Furthermore, I pray that the blind may regain their sight, the deaf may regain their hearing, the mute may be able to speak, the naked may obtain clothing, and those who are poor and destitute may find a treasury of jewels; may their storehouses overflow so that they lack for nothing, and may all receive peace and happiness, until not even a single person suffers."

"Furthermore, I vow that sentient beings shall face one another with hearts of loving-kindness and gaze upon each other with the Buddha-eye; their physical forms shall be upright and dignified, pleasing to all who behold them, and their bodies shall be adorned with supreme and wondrous features, serving as true spiritual friends for the retinue of Bodhi."
In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Questions and Answers on Retribution for Śramaṇas by Padmadarśana*, it is said that shortly thereafter, Padmadarśana further entered the Flesh-Tearing Hell.
Why is it called the Flesh-Tearing Hell?

That hell is forty *yojanas* in length and breadth; it is surrounded on all sides by iron walls and covered above with an iron net, with smoke and fire blazing together no differently than described above.
The ground is paved with iron spikes and the fire also blazes intensely. Within it is an iron bed, five hundred paces square, upon which fire blazes forth to burn the offenders.
In the middle of the southern gate were six hundred sinners; they resembled human forms but were not humans, being one zhang in height and lacking mouths, eyes, hands, feet, or the six sense organs.
At that time, the horse-headed rākṣasa grasped an iron hook in his hand and prodded him toward his body.
As the sinner’s body moved, it sounded like a human voice as he cried out these words:
"For what sin do I now undergo such suffering?"

The hell-wardens seize his body and drag him into the prison. Within the prison, iron spikes point upward and pierce his body; blood flows from his limbs as fire enters within. Furthermore, hungry ghosts come to devour his flesh;

hungry dogs come to drink his blood; iron crows come to peck at his sinews; and fierce winds come to blow upon the sinner. Day and night he undergoes ten thousand kinds of suffering, dying and being reborn a thousand times, ten thousand times.
If they obtain a human birth, they will be poor, impoverished, and mired in ignorance,
failing to recognize the Buddha’s words. Bodhidhara asked the Horse-Headed Rākṣasa,
"What sins did these śramaṇas commit that they undergo such suffering?"

The horse-headed rākṣasa replied, "These śramaṇas received the prohibitory precepts of the Buddha, yet they did not seek unsurpassed bodhi; instead, they sought only fame and profit in the present life. Because they greedily drank alcohol, they violated the Dharma and broke the precepts, resulting in thirty-six faults.
By these causes and conditions, they have fallen into this hell."
Upon hearing this, Baoda wept with grief and departed.

At that time, the bhikṣus addressed the Buddha, saying:
Are the lifespans of all these Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, equal in length and brevity?"
"Monks! One kalpa in this Sahā world, the buddha-field of Śākyamuni Buddha of the Bhadrakalpa, constitutes a single day and night in the world of Sukhāvatī."
"One eon in the land of Amitābha Buddha in the world Sukhāvatī is equivalent to one day and night in the land of Vajrapramardana Buddha in the world Kāṣāyadhvaja."
"One eon in the world-system Kāṣāyadhvaja constitutes a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Padmavyūhadeha-sukhābha-prabhāsa, in the world-system Avivartacakranirghoṣa."
"One eon in the world-system Avivartyacakranirghoṣa is a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Dharmadhvaja in the world-system Vimalā."
"One eon in the world-system Vimalā is but a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Siṃha in the world-system Supratīṣṭhadīpa.
One eon in the world-system Supratīṣṭhadīpa is but a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Vairocanagarbha in the world-system Suprabhā."
“One eon in the world-system of Good Radiance constitutes a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Dharma-Radiance Padma-Adorned Body in the world-system Difficult to Transcend.”
"If one *kalpa* in the world Difficult to Traverse were to constitute a single day and night in the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata Universal Radiance of Adorned Wisdom."
"One eon in the world-system Adorned Wisdom is a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Moon-Wisdom in the world-system Mirror-Disk Radiance."

“Bhikṣus! Entering into such a calculation, it takes as many worlds as ten hundred thousand koṭis of asaṃkhyeyas to reach the final world, Padmottara-vijaya; in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī, that constitutes one day and night.”
“Monks! Just as these worlds are immeasurable and boundless, with varying lengths and durations, so too is the lifespan of the Tathāgatas as they abide in the world.”

"O Bhikṣus! You should all recite the names of these Buddhas—[in the Hu-ben [Sanskrit original], from this point onward there are names of world-systems, which have been omitted here for brevity]—and speak thus:
'Namo to these and all other Tathāgatas.'"

"I take refuge in all such immeasurable and boundless great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
I pay homage to all the worthy and holy ones, including Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas."

“Homage to the Venerable Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra; homage to the Venerable Vīradatta; homage to the Venerable Upāli; homage to the Venerable Kṣemaka; homage to the Venerable Aniruddha; homage to the Venerable Revata; homage to the Venerable Śāriputra; homage to the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana; homage to the Venerable Ānanda; homage to the Venerable Rāhula. I take refuge in these and all other great Arhats who are widely known.”
"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next perform repentance. Disciples!

Having already repented for all retributions, we shall now once again collectively and universally repent for all transgressions, earnestly entreating the Buddhas of the ten directions to protect and deliver us, their disciples."

Since beginningless, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas past, we have committed evil karmas that cannot be fully recounted—whether by committing the ten non-virtuous actions, the five heinous crimes, or slandering the Vaipulya sutras; or by creating immeasurable asaṃkhyeya offenses. We now take refuge in the Buddhas of the ten directions, we take refuge in the Dharma of the ten directions, and we take refuge in the Sangha of the ten directions.

"Next, I again take refuge and prostrate myself before Akṣobhya Buddha of the east, Ratnaketu Buddha of the south, Amitābha Buddha of the west, Supuṣpacandra Buddha of the north, Sugandhakūṭa Tathāgata of the zenith, and Koṭirāja Buddha of the nadir."

"I prostrate to the Great Being Samantabhadra of the east, the Great Being Lokadhara of the south, the Great Being Avalokiteśvara of the west, the Great Being Pūrṇacandra of the north, the Great Being Gaganagañja of the zenith, and the Great Being Dṛḍhaśrī of the nadir; I take refuge in the Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha and in the buddha-nature of future Buddhas."
"Furthermore, I prostrate to the transformation Buddhas who manifest as emanations in other directions, and to the Great Beings Vimalakīrti and Mañjuśrī.
I also prostrate to Ānanda, Kāśyapa, and the noble ones who appear within the four paths."

"I also take refuge in the initial teachings of the Dharma; I bow my head in homage to the twelve divisions of the Great Canon, as well as to other sūtras, the Vaipulya scriptures, and the eightfold reliquary images."

"I also take refuge in all those who currently perform Buddha-deeds; in the Four Heavenly Kings; in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, including Śakra and Brahmā; and in all the ṛṣis throughout the heavens, upon the earth, and beneath the earth, wherever they dwell among the mountains, forests, and trees."
There are those with great supernormal powers, those with the divine eye, and those with the divine ear; I pray that you grant me your hearing and knowledge to serve as witnesses for all.
May all sentient beings who have not yet repented, upon performing this repentance, attain the eradication of their transgressions.
Disciple! Today, in repentance, I strip away my heart and expose my gallbladder to take refuge with utmost sincerity in the Buddha.

Homage to Akṣobhyajñāna Buddha of the East. Homage to Candrasūryapradīpa Buddha of the South. Homage to Viśeṣa Buddha of the West. Homage to Guṇakoṭisamalaṃkṛtarāja Buddha of the North. Homage to Siṃhamati Buddha of the Southeast. Homage to Ratnāvabhāsagaganaprabhāsa Buddha of the Southwest. Homage to Vigatabhayadarśana Buddha of the Northwest. Homage to Siṃhabala Buddha of the Northeast. Homage to Vicikitsācchedanarāgoddharaṇatamopagata Buddha of the Nadir. Homage to Suvarṇaratnāvabhāsa Buddha of the Zenith. I take refuge in all the Triple Gem throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of empty space.

"Disciples! Since beginningless time throughout the world, and continuing until now, this evil body has been deluded and the mind distracted; the immeasurable inverted views, afflictions, and evil karmas cannot be fully recounted. We have committed various sins without realizing it ourselves, our evil intentions burning fiercely as we failed to perceive the next world."

They see only the present cultivation of pleasure, the distancing of the roots of goodness through the afflictions, the obstruction of evil karma, and proximity to evil associates; or they commit unrighteous acts toward bhikṣus, unrighteous acts toward bhikṣuṇīs, unrighteous acts toward their parents, or again, unrighteous acts before the great assembly.

"Or again, they may willfully misappropriate the property of the Saṃgha; or they may commit right or wrong against the fivefold assembly of monks; or they may speak of the immeasurable evil fruits of the world; or they may kill sentient beings who possess the roots of bodhi; or they may slander Dharma masters, declaring the Dharma to be non-Dharma and non-Dharma to be Dharma."
That is to say, we have held that the Tathāgata is impermanent, the True Dharma is impermanent, and the Sangha Jewel is impermanent; we took no delight in giving and instead accepted false teachings.

Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless. For this reason, today we feel immeasurable fear and immeasurable shame and remorse. We take refuge in the Triple Gem, the compassionate Buddhas, the Vaipulya sutras, our parents, the Bodhisattvas, and our spiritual friends, and request their permission for us to now openly confess and repent.

"Disciples! Since immeasurable kalpas past, you have committed the five heinous crimes, or violated the prohibitions and precepts of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present; you have acted as icchantikas, uttering coarse words to slander the True Dharma, and having created such grave karma, you have never repented or reformed, lacking any sense of shame or remorse."

Or, having committed such offenses as the ten evil deeds, they know for certain that they have committed such grave matters; yet from the beginning, their minds were devoid of fear, shame, or remorse. They silently accepted offerings without ever confessing them, lacking any intention to protect, cherish, or establish the True Dharma, and in the meantime, they disparaged and belittled it with many words of fault and evil.
Or again, some may say that the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha do not exist; or they may lack faith in the existence of various hells where retribution is received.

Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless. Today, with immeasurable fear and immeasurable shame, we take refuge in the Triple Gem, the compassionate Buddhas, the Vaipulya sutras, our parents, the Bodhisattvas, and our spiritual friends. We request your permission to openly confess and repent.

"Disciples! From immeasurable kalpas past until this very day, you have sometimes held the four inverted views; you have spoken of the four grave offenses as *sthūlātyaya*, and spoken of *sthūlātyaya* offenses as the four grave offenses; you have declared what was an offense to be no offense, and what was not an offense to be an offense; you have called a light sin heavy, and a heavy sin light; you have viewed the pure as impure, and the impure as pure."

Furthermore, some hold wrong views, praising worldly treatises while showing no respect for the Buddha’s sutras; they engage in various evil discourses, keep the eight kinds of impure things, regarding what is truly the Buddha’s word as the Mara’s word, and what is truly the Mara’s word as the Buddha’s word.
Or again, some may believe and accept what the six teachers have said, or they may say:
"The Tathāgata has today entered parinirvāṇa; the Three Jewels are impermanent.
Thus, their bodies and minds give rise to delusions and immeasurable inverted views.

"Therefore, today, filled with immeasurable fear and immeasurable shame and remorse, we take refuge in the Three Jewels, the compassion of all Buddhas, the Vaipulya sutras, our parents, and our bodhisattva spiritual friends; please grant us permission to openly confess and repent."

"May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession, vow that in every birth and throughout all lifetimes, we shall rescue and deliver all sentient beings of the ten directions; may they distance themselves from the ten unwholesome actions and practice the ten wholesome paths; may all who suffer find peace and stability; and may inconceivable numbers of *asaṃkhyeya* beings be established in the ten stages (*bhūmi*)."
I dedicate all wholesome dharmas found in this land and in all other worlds.

May the merit of the good deeds of body, speech, and mind that I have cultivated lead me to realize the Unsurpassed Way in a future life. May all women become men, endowed with wisdom and diligent without slackening, so that they may all practice the path of the Bodhisattva and zealously cultivate and accumulate the six *pāramitās*.

"Whatever various, virtuous, and sublime merits have been performed by all sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa and in immeasurable worlds in other directions, I now rejoice in them with a profound heart."

By means of these merits of sympathetic joy, as well as the wholesome deeds performed by my body, speech, and mind, I vow that in future lives I shall attain the Unsurpassed Way and obtain the pure, stainless, and auspicious fruits of retribution, fully realizing the perfect enlightenment of a Tathāgata.
In the *Mahāyāna Padma-ratna-bodhi-praśna-pratyaya-śramaṇa-sūtra*, Bodhi entered yet another hell called the Hell of the Burning Body (*kāya-jvalana-naraka*).
Why is it named the Hell of the Burning Body?

That hell is fifty yojanas in length and breadth; it is surrounded on all sides by iron walls from which fierce flames blaze forth to burn the sinners. The bodies of the sinners are likewise set ablaze, and smoke and fire issue forth from every pore of their skin.
Within the eastern gate were eight hundred sinners who entered therein, crying out with loud voices and beating their own bodies, saying:
"For what crime have we now come to enter this place?"

The horse-headed rākṣasa grasps a three-pronged iron trident with his hand and strikes it against the [sinner’s] back; it pierces through to emerge from his chest. He enters therein where fire blazes upon the ground; fire within his body likewise blazes forth, and flames stream out from his six sense organs. For one day and one night he undergoes immeasurable suffering, unable to seek life and unable to seek death.
Bao Da asked the horse-headed rākṣasa,
"What sins have these śramaṇas committed to suffer such torment?
"These śramaṇas are either teachers or disciples who do not accord with one another; the teacher is not compassionate toward the disciple, and the disciple does not respect the teacher."
Each harboring mutual hatred, they cried out in loud voices, glaring with eyes of rage as they vied and contended; thus giving rise to enmity and loathing, they fell into this hell.
Emerging from hell, they encountered one another life after life, constantly killing and harming each other.
Upon hearing this, Baoda wept with grief and departed.

Homage to the *Dhyānaguhya-uttara-dharma*. "I pay homage to all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the ten directions.
