"Disciples! From time immemorial until this very day, you have engaged in false speech, double-tongued speech, harsh speech, and frivolous speech; you have reported the empty as existing and described the existent as empty; you have said you saw what you did not see, and said you did not see what you had seen; you have said you heard what you did not hear, and said you did not hear what you had heard; you have claimed to know what you did not know, and claimed not to know what you did know; you have deceived the worthy and misled the sages, such that your words and deeds were in mutual contradiction."

They praise themselves, claiming to have attained superhuman states: "I have attained the four dhyānas, the four formless absorptions, and the sixteenfold contemplation of ānāpāna; I have attained the fruits from srotāpanna up to arhatship; I am a pratyekabuddha or a non-retrogressive bodhisattva. They claim that devas, nāgas, ghosts, spirits, whirlwinds, and earth-demons all come to their presence; they answer the questions posed by these beings to manifest wonders and delude the masses, seeking worldly fame and profit.
Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless; today we reveal them, take refuge, and repent.

From beginningless time until this day, we have engaged in slanderous speech to incite strife and foment discord between others; we have practiced double-tonguedness and malicious scheming, trafficking in idle talk. We have reported what was said here to those there, and what was said there to those here, alienating others' retinues, destroying marriages and kinships, and exhausting others with our verbal machinations.
They speak of others' long and short faults, destroying their virtuous friends; they cause those who were close and intimate to become estranged, and turn former kin into enemies.

Sometimes they engage in frivolous speech that is untrue and fails to reach the meaning; they slander rulers and fathers, disparage teachers and elders, ruin the loyal and good, and bury those who surpass them. They act as intermediaries between two states, fanning discord on both sides; their words are flowery and vainly clever, always empty in substance. Their mouths agree with their hearts in falsehood; their paths are manifold. They praise and extol someone to one's face, yet revile and destroy them behind one's back; they recite heterodox books and propagate evil, heretical teachings.
Whether through harsh speech, verbal abuse, or coarse and violent language, or by calling upon heaven, pointing at the earth, or invoking spirits and deities—

regarding all such immeasurable and boundless transgressions born of the karma of speech, I today, with utmost sincerity, take refuge and repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Assembly of Sages.

“May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession of offenses committed through verbal karma and the like, in every birth and every life, possess the eight qualities of vocal sound and the four types of unimpeded eloquence; may we always speak words that are harmonious and beneficial, with voices so pure and elegant that all delight in hearing them, and may we skillfully understand the various dialects and languages of sentient beings.”

If one speaks that which is timely and appropriate to the occasion, causing those who hear it to attain understanding and realization, they shall transcend the mundane and enter the sacred, opening the eye of wisdom.
In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Concerning Retribution for Śramaṇas*, the Jewel-Penetrating One (Bao-da) entered a Hell of Disputes just a moment before.
What is called the Hell of Contentious Disputation?

This hell is eighty yojanas in length and breadth; it is surrounded on all sides by iron walls and covered above with a network of iron mesh, and within it there are iron spikes as previously described.

Within it, iron hooks hook the tongues of the sinners; furthermore, iron axes come to hack their tongues, severing them inch by inch. Again, glowing molten lead is poured into their mouths and emerges from their backs. Day and night they undergo immeasurable suffering, dying ten thousand times and being reborn ten thousand times, dying a thousand times and being reborn a thousand times.
Within the Western Gate, six thousand śramaṇas came to enter it, but the sinners wailed and refused to go inside.

The horse-headed rākṣasa, grasping an iron fork in his hand, thrust it through their chests so that it emerged from their backs as they entered; meanwhile, iron birds flew down from high and descended into the place.
When the sinner raises his head, [the fire] enters through his mouth and exits from beneath his feet; furthermore, pythons enter his eyes, and flames burn within his body.
Bodhidatta asked, "What karma did these śramaṇas commit to come here and undergo such punishment?"

"These śramaṇas have received the Buddha’s prohibitions and precepts but do not guard them for the future; they claim, 'I am a Dharma teacher of the Mahāyāna. Yet, it is as if it were the dead of night: each speaks of themselves, saying, 'I have attained a profound understanding of the Buddha-dharma,' and thus they preach the meaning of the Buddha's teachings to others."

They merely lead the multitude on tours through the human world, or receive the faithful offerings and support of kings; yet within their hearts, they harbor a sense of self as vast as mountains and seas.
They are like withered trees that possess only their bark, while the core is rotten and useless;
these śramaṇas are just like this.
"By these causes and conditions, one falls into this hell; upon emerging from the hell, if one is born among humans, one will be deaf, blind, and mute, unable to hear the True Dharma.
Hearing this, Bodhidharma wept with sorrow and departed.

"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next perform repentance. Disciples!
Having already repented for the three types of bodily and four types of verbal transgressions, we now further repent for all obstacles between ourselves and the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha."
Therefore, it is said in the sutras: "A human body is difficult to obtain;

the Buddha-dharma is difficult to hear; the Sangha is difficult to encounter; faith is difficult to give rise to; the six sense faculties are difficult to possess in full; virtuous friends are difficult to find; and a mind of dread is difficult to arouse."

"Yet now, having together planted roots of goodness in past lives, we have obtained this human body with its six faculties complete; furthermore, having encountered virtuous friends, we have been able to hear the True Dharma. Within this interval, if each of us again fails to apply ourselves with wholehearted diligence, I fear that in the future we shall sink long into myriad sufferings with no time of escape."

"Disciples! From beginningless time until this very day, our minds have been constantly shrouded by ignorance and the hindrances of affliction have been heavy. Or they may reside in a magnificent hall themselves while installing the honored image in a lowly and filthy place, subjecting it to smoke, sun, wind, rain, and dew; it becomes defiled by dust and excrement, ruined by sparrows and rats, and they dwell and sleep alongside it without ever showing it reverence.
Some have left the physical form of the Buddha exposed and naked, never adorning it; others have obscured the lamps and candles, closing the halls and obstructing the Buddha’s radiance.

Some leave them placed at the head of their beds, neither sitting up nor rising with respect; some shut them away in chests and boxes where they are eaten by insects and rot; some have their binding cords fallen out and the sections disordered; some are incomplete, missing, or erroneous, with paper and ink cracked and broken; yet they do not repair them themselves and refuse to circulate them.

"Whether sleeping on the ground while listening to the sutras, or reciting them while lying on one's back; speaking loudly or making noise to disturb others who are listening to the Dharma; or misinterpreting the Buddha’s words and explaining the intent of the teachings perversely; preaching what is not the Dharma as the Dharma, and preaching the Dharma as not the Dharma; declaring what is not an offense to be an offense, and declaring an offense to be no offense; speaking of light offenses as heavy, and speaking of heavy offenses as light."

Such offenses as these, the immeasurable and boundless karmic obstructions arising against the Triple Gem, I now, with utmost sincerity, repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Assembly of Sages, taking refuge and confessing them all.

In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Concerning Retribution for Śramaṇas*, as Precious Attainment was about to enter yet another hell-field known as the Hell of Plowing, he asked:
"Why is this hell called the Hell of Plowing?"

That hell is twenty yojanas in length and breadth; it is surrounded on all sides by iron walls with fierce, blazing fires, where the flames from above penetrate below and those from below penetrate above, such that the conflagration blazes intensely and the smoke and fire are vividly radiant.

At that time, iron blades sprang up from the ground within the prison; their edges pointed upward, and flames blazed forth from them to burn the offenders. In their frantic panic, the offenders' spirits were scattered and their souls were terrified; they were so bewildered and distressed by the gloom that they remained unaware of themselves, enduring thousands of forms of punishment and billions of agonies.
Within that hell, there are iron oxen that plow the ground, from which flames arise simultaneously.
Within the eastern gate are six thousand sinners; fire blazes from their mouths and eyes, smoke and flames erupt together, and fire flows from their hands, bodies, and six sense organs like water.

The sinner, a śramaṇa, refuses to move forward; the horse-headed rākṣasa seizes an iron fork with his hand and thrusts it through his back so that it emerges from his chest. He seizes an iron hook with his hand and reaches for his skeleton, advancing step by step. Amidst this, iron dogs come to drink his blood, and hungry ghosts come to devour his flesh.

At that time, the sinful śramaṇas take iron plows in their hands and plow the ground; the ground blazes with fire as it flows along, and the furrows raised by the plows likewise flow with fire to burn the sinners. The grain and weeds growing from the earth are also ablaze with fire. Day and night, they die ten thousand times and are reborn ten thousand times, undergoing great suffering and affliction. Their spirits wander like drifting waves and their souls dwell in the dark abyss; only after passing through thousands of millions of kalpas do they finally obtain human form, yet they are deaf, blind, mute, and loathed by others. They are unjustly entangled in legal affairs and imprisoned by the local authorities, and foul sores break out upon their bodies as they roam the wilds.
Bao Da asked the horse-headed rākṣasa,
"What kind of conduct did these śramaṇas practice that they now undergo such suffering?

"These śramaṇas, though they receive the prohibitions and precepts of the Buddha, do not fear the three evil realms or the eight difficult conditions. To plow fields and plant crops is called breaking the precepts; they prepare their own food with their own hands and eat what they have gathered themselves, even killing plants and trees. They are just like the outcaste *caṇḍālas* and other heretics, devoid of any sense of shame or remorse."
"By these causes and conditions, one falls into this hell.

I have already repented of the affliction-obstructions (*kleśāvaraṇa*) and the karma-obstructions (*karmāvaraṇa*). Now, I shall sequentially disclose and repent of the remaining retribution-obstructions (*vipākāvaraṇa*).
As it is said in the Sūtras:

"When the retribution of karma arrives, there is no escape—neither in the void, nor in the midst of the ocean, nor by entering between mountain rocks; there is no other place where one may avoid receiving the retribution. Only through the power of repentance can it be extinguished."
"How is this known to be so?

When Śakra Devānām-indra manifested the five signs of decline, his heart was overcome with fear as he took refuge with sincerity in the Triple Gem; the signs of death were immediately extinguished, and he obtained an extension of his celestial lifespan."
In this manner, the matters clarified by the scriptural teachings are not limited to these alone; thus, we know that repentance truly has the power to extinguish calamity.

However, if ordinary persons do not encounter the guidance and encouragement of virtuous friends, there is no evil they will not commit. Consequently, when their great life is about to end and they face the brink of death, the horrific manifestations of hell appear before them.

At that time, remorse and fear will converge; failing to cultivate goodness beforehand, one only regrets when facing the ultimate end. What can such subsequent regret avail? Calamities and misfortunes await in their respective places, prepared long ago;

one must enter alone and travel far to another realm. When one has already stepped forward into the great cauldron, with body and mind shattered and spirit in agony, how could one possibly seek even a single prostration or a single confession at such a moment?

Do not rely on your own youth, wealth, treasures, or power, nor indulge in indolence, laziness, negligence, and self-indulgence. When the suffering of death arrives, it leaves nothing behind—whether one is old or young, poor or rich, noble or humble—and all are utterly extinguished. It comes suddenly and unexpectedly, such that no one can know it is coming."
Life is impermanent, like the morning dew; though the outgoing breath may enter, the incoming breath is difficult to preserve. Why, then, do you not repent?

Furthermore, once the five divine messengers have arrived and the demon of impermanence has suddenly descended, even those in the prime of youth and vigor cannot escape. At such a time, what concern would magnificent halls and deep chambers have for human affairs?
"How could these tall carriages and large horses follow me? My wife, children, and kinsmen are no longer my kin; these ornaments of the seven precious gems have become the playthings of others.
From this it may be seen that the retributions of the world are all like illusions and transformations."
"Though the heavens above are pleasant, they ultimately end in decay; when one's lifespan is exhausted, the soul falls into the three miserable realms. Therefore, the Buddha said to Subhadra:

'Your teacher Udraka Rāmaputra possessed sharp faculties and intelligence, and was able to subdue his afflictions; yet upon reaching the Sphere of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception, at the end of his life he was reborn as a flying weasel within the animal realm—how much more so for others? "
Thus, one should know that until the fruit of sainthood is realized, all must continue to transmigrate and fully experience the miserable realms.
If one is not careful, one may suddenly and unexpectedly encounter such calamity in a single day, leaving no time for regret.

Suppose, for instance, that one is now being led to the public court on charges of a crime; this is already a minor suffering, yet the spirit is terrified and the kinsfolk are filled with dread, seeking rescue by every possible means. Compared to this, the manifold sufferings of the hells are hundreds of thousands of millions of times greater, such that no analogy can suffice.

Since we have been together through successive kalpas, our sins are as vast as Mount Sumeru. How is it that upon hearing this, you remain so composed, neither fearing, nor trembling, nor being terrified?
To cause these spirits to once again suffer such agony is truly a matter for lamentation."
Therefore, disciples! Mobilizing this sincere devotion, take refuge in the Buddha with a devoted heart.

“Disciples! From time immemorial until this very day, among all karmic obstacles of retribution, the most grave is none other than the Avīci Hell. As clarified in the sutras, I shall now briefly describe its characteristics.”

This hell is surrounded on all sides by seven layers of iron cities, further covered above by seven layers of iron nets; below, there are seven layers of sword-forests and immeasurable fierce fires, extending eighty-four thousand yojanas in length and breadth.

The bodies of the sinners fill the entire space, yet their karmic conditions do not obstruct one another. The upper fires penetrate downward and the lower fires penetrate upward; they pass through and intersect from east to west and south to north. Just as when fish are being fried in a cauldron until their fat and grease are entirely consumed, so too is the suffering of sin within this place.

"At the four gates of that city are four great copper dogs; their bodies are forty yojanas in length and breadth, with fangs and claws as sharp and formidable as spears, and eyes like flashes of lightning.

Furthermore, there are immeasurable birds with iron beaks that fly and soar about, pecking at the flesh of the offenders. The ox-headed hell-wardens have forms like rākṣasas, each possessing nine tails, with tails resembling iron forks."

Furthermore, there are eight heads, each with eighteen horns and sixty-four eyes; from every single eye, iron balls burst forth, scorching the flesh of the sinners. Whenever they grow enraged and roar in fury, their sound is like a thunderclap.

Furthermore, immeasurable natural wheels of blades descend from the air, entering through the crowns of the sinners' heads and exiting through their feet; thus, the pain of these sinners penetrates to the very marrow of their bones, cutting through their livers and hearts with agonizing intensity.
Thus, for immeasurable years, they have undergone various sufferings and afflictions, unable to seek birth and unable to seek death.
For all such retributions, today we prostrate ourselves with our heads to the ground, feeling shame and remorse, and sincerely confess and repent.
"I repent for the retribution of my crimes in the remaining hells: the hells of the mountain of knives and the forest of swords, where my body and head were severed;
the hells of the boiling cauldrons and the burning embers, where I was scorched and cooked;
and the hells of the iron bed and the copper pillar, where I was consumed by flames."
I repent for the retribution of being split and crushed in the Hell of the Wheel of Blades and the Fiery Chariot;
I repent for the retribution of agony and pain in the Hell of the Plow-tilling of Tongues;
I repent for the retribution of the five internal organs being consumed and rotted in the Hell of Swallowing Iron Balls and Pouring Molten Copper into the Mouth.
I repent for the retribution of my sins that resulted in the Iron Mortar and Iron Grinding Hell, where my bones and flesh were ground into dust;
I repent for the retribution of my sins that resulted in the Black Rope and Iron Net Hell, where my limbs and joints were torn asunder.
I repent for the retribution of suffering and distress in the Ash River and Boiling Excrement Hells;
I repent for the retribution of having one's skin split open and being nakedly frozen in the Salt Water and Cold Water Hells;
and I repent for the retribution of mutual slaughter and injury in the Hells of Tigers, Wolves, Hawks, and Dogs.
I repent for the retribution of the Hell of Weapons and Blades, where beings strike, seize, hack, and stab one another;
I repent for the retribution of the Hell of Fire Pits, where they are roasted and broiled;
I repent for the retribution of the Hell of Crushing Between Two Rocks, where their physical forms are shattered to pieces.
In the Samghāta Black-Ear Hell, one repents for the retribution of being dismembered;
in the Andhatamas Flesh-Mountain Hell, one repents for the retribution of being hacked and minced;
in the Hell of Saws and Nails, one repents for the retribution of being severed and cut.
I repent for the retribution of being butchered and dismembered in the Hell of the Upside-Down Iron Staff;
I repent for the retribution of grievous resentment in the Hells of Intense Heat and Screaming;
I repent for the retribution of not recognizing the three luminaries amidst the perpetual darkness between the Great and Small Iron Ring Mountains.

The Āpāpa hell, the Āśāśa hell, the Aṭaṭa hell, and the Alalā hell—thus, within all these eight cold and eight hot hells, each individual hell further has eighty-four thousand subsidiary hells as its retinue. Within these, the suffering of punishment and torment, the agony of being boiled and roasted, the flaying of skin, the hacking away of flesh, the carving of bones, the beating of marrow, the extraction of intestines, and the pulling out of lungs—these immeasurable sufferings are such that they cannot be heard and cannot be described.

Those who are here within this place today may well have been our parents or all our kinsmen throughout our beginningless cycle of births. After we pass away, we too shall surely fall into such a hell as this.”

Today, with a purified mind and utmost sincerity, I prostrate myself, knocking my head against the ground before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas of the great earth, entreating their compassion for repentance, so that all these karmic obstacles of retribution may be utterly extinguished.

"May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession of retributions for the hells and other realms, pray that in every birth and every life, the compassion of all Buddhas may rescue sentient beings from suffering, immediately shattering the iron city of Avīci, so that it becomes entirely like the Pure Land, where even the name of the evil paths does not exist."

In all other hells, every instrument of suffering was transformed into a condition for bliss; the mountains of knives and trees of swords became forests of jewels; the boiling cauldrons and burning coals were transformed into lotus blossoms from which beings were born; the ox-headed jailers abandoned their cruelty and arose in compassion, free from any evil intent; the sentient beings in hell attained liberation from the fruits of suffering and ceased to create further causes, experiencing equal peace and happiness as if in the third dhyāna, and simultaneously gave rise to the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment.

In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Regarding Retribution for Śramaṇas* concerning the Jewel-Attaining [Śramaṇa], the Jewel-Attainer shortly thereafter entered an Iron Fire House Hell.
Why is it called the Iron House Hell?

That hell is thirty-four yojanas in length and breadth; it is surrounded on all sides by iron walls and covered above by an iron lattice. At the four corners of the iron city, fierce winds blow violently against it, causing the iron city to tremble and naturally emit fire, which blazes intensely throughout the entire prison.

Furthermore, there are iron spikes as sharp as the points of awls, suspended in mid-air, making a deep, grating sound like the roar of thunder; these spikes descend in a chaotic flurry, piercing the bodies of the offenders.

There is a great iron bed, more than forty paces in circumference, surrounded by a fire-house; the bodies of the offenders are spread across this bed, and whatever retributions they undergo are entirely without obstruction.
At that time, within the western gate, there were immeasurable and boundless sinners who cried out these words:
"By what transgression have we now entered this place?"
Striking his own body with both hands, he stumbles and rolls about, wailing and crying out in grief, refusing to move forward.

The horse-headed rākṣasa seizes him with iron tongs and, clamping them against his chest, hurls him into the hell; wherever the tongs touch, smoke and flames erupt together. The yakṣa wardens strike him on the head with great iron hooks and drag him into an iron house of fire.
The house is surrounded on all sides by fierce, blazing flames; driven by the power of their karma, the bodies of these offenders are made to mount a bed and lie there.
Great venomous snakes with scales like spikes enter through their mouths and emerge from below;
furthermore, iron birds peck at their hearts, tearing out their hearts and entrails.
Such suffering is unbearable; for one day and one night, they undergo immeasurable punishment, seeking life but unable to find it, seeking death but unable to find it.

Only after passing through thousands of millions of kalpas do they finally gain release. Upon emerging from hell, they shall become animals, yoked to plows and burdened with heavy loads to repay their past debts, enduring this through hundreds and thousands of lifetimes without rest.
Bao Da asked the Horse-Headed Rākṣasa,
"By what offenses did these various sinners arrive here, that they undergo such suffering?

"These śramaṇas have received the pure precepts of the Buddha but do not maintain them; they go toward laypeople and sleep in dwellings that were not offered to them. Because of this, they give rise to thoughts of desire, defiling bhikṣus of pure conduct and bhikṣuṇīs, and they steal the property of the Saṃgha."

Because of these sins, one falls into this hell; later, if one obtains human form, one shall fall into the five heinous crimes. One's family will be poor, cold, and lowly, with tattered clothing that does not even cover the body; having no home of one's own, one dwells exposed to the wind and rain.
Upon hearing this, Baoda wept and said:
"How can one who is called a world-transcender be bound by the mundane?
Having attained the gates of liberation, why is he instead oppressed by desire?"
Having spoken these words, he departed weeping.

"Disciples! We have already finished repenting for the retribution of the hells; now we shall further repent for the retribution of the three evil realms.
As the Buddha said in the sutras:"
"One who has many desires seeks much profit, and therefore suffers much affliction.
One who knows contentment finds joy even while lying upon the ground; one who lacks contentment is dissatisfied even when dwelling in heaven."

Yet when worldly people suddenly encounter urgent distress, they are able to relinquish their wealth without regard for its quantity; they do not realize, however, that this body stands upon the edge of the deep pits of the three miserable realms, and that with a single breath not returned, it will surely fall.
Suddenly, a spiritual friend instructs one to cultivate merit and to prepare the provisions for wholesome dharmas in the future; yet, clinging to this stingy mind, one refuses to act accordingly.
Such a person is utterly foolish and deluded.
Why is this so? In the sutras, the Buddha said:

"At birth, one does not bring a single coin; at death, one does not take a single coin away. One exhausts the body through accumulation, resulting only in anxiety and distress. It benefits oneself not at all but serves only as the property of others. Having no goodness to rely upon and no virtue to depend on, one’s life ends in falling into the various evil realms."
"Therefore, disciples! Today, with utmost sincerity, prostrating yourselves with heads to the ground and with earnest, heartfelt devotion, take refuge in the Buddha:

Namo to the Buddha High Radiance of the East; Namo to the Buddha Supreme Lotus of the South; Namo to the Buddha King of Great Compassionate Radiance of the West; Namo to the Buddha Flower Mountain Treasury of the North; Namo to the Buddha Sound of the Buddha’s Voice of the Southeast; Namo to the Buddha Udumbara Flower Banner of the Southwest; Namo to the Buddha Turning Auspiciousness of the Northwest; Namo to the Buddha Pure Radiant Illumination of the Northeast; Namo to the Buddha Without Retrogression or Decline of the Nadir; Namo to the Buddha Jewel Virtue Steps of the Zenith. We take refuge in all the Triple Gems throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the realm of empty space."
"Disciples! Today we further repent for the retribution of our sins consisting of ignorance within the realm of animals;
we repent for the retribution of our sins consisting of carrying heavy loads, pulling plows, and repaying past debts to others within the realm of animals."
I repent for the karmic retribution of being unable to attain self-mastery within the realm of animals, being hacked, pierced, slaughtered, and dismembered by others;
I repent for the karmic retribution of having no feet, two feet, four feet, or many feet within the realm of animals;
I repent for the karmic retribution of having my body’s various hairs, feathers, scales, and shells eaten away by tiny insects within the realm of animals.
We repent for such immeasurable and boundless retributions for sins within the animal realm; today, with utmost sincerity, we take refuge and repent.
Today, I further repent for the retribution of long-term hunger within the realm of hungry ghosts;
I repent for the retribution of never having heard the names of even water or gruel for hundreds of thousands of myriads of years within the realm of hungry ghosts;
I repent for the retribution of consuming pus, blood, excrement, and filth within the realm of hungry ghosts.
I repent for the retribution of my sins wherein, while moving the body within the realm of hungry ghosts, every limb and joint was entirely ablaze;
I repent for the retribution of my sins wherein, within the realm of hungry ghosts, the belly was vast and the throat was narrow.
We repent for such immeasurable and boundless retributions of suffering within the realm of hungry ghosts; therefore, today we prostrate with utmost sincerity, taking refuge and repenting.
Today, we further repent for the karmic retribution of flattery, deceit, and false claims within the realms of all ghosts, spirits, and asuras;
we repent for the karmic retribution of carrying sand and bearing stones, filling rivers and blocking seas, within the realm of ghosts and spirits;
and we repent for the karmic retribution of being born with such ugliness as to devour flesh and blood raw, among the various evil ghosts and spirits such as yakṣas and kumbhāṇḍas.

I repent of all such immeasurable and boundless retributions for sins within the realm of ghosts and spirits; today, with my head bowed to the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas of the great earth, I seek their compassion and repent so that they may all be extinguished.

"May we disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this repentance for the retribution of animal births and the like, vow that in every life and every age we shall extinguish the defilement of ignorance, recognize our own karmic conditions, illuminate with the light of wisdom, and sever the body of the evil realms."

By the merit arising from this confession of the retributions of hungry ghosts and others, may we, in birth after birth throughout all lifetimes, forever be free from the suffering of stinginess, greed, hunger, and thirst, and always partake of the nectar-like flavor of liberation.

By the merit produced through this repentance for the retributions of ghosts, spirits, and asuras, I vow that in every birth and lifetime I shall be upright and sincere, free from flattery; that I may depart from the causes of wrong livelihood and eliminate the fruits of ugliness, thereby bringing benefit and welfare to humans and devas.

May we, the disciples, from this day forth until we reach the site of enlightenment, certainly not receive the retribution of the four evil realms; except only when, out of great compassion for sentient beings, we dwell therein through the power of our vows without weariness.
In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Concerning Retribution for Śramaṇas*, as Precious Attainment was about to enter another hell called the Hell of Burial Under Ruins, he asked:
"Why is it named the Hell of Burial Under Ruins?"

That hell is forty-nine yojanas in length and breadth, surrounded by an iron city. At the four corners of the iron city are mountains of diamond; when powerful winds blow, they strike the mountains together, grinding them into fine powder until there is not even a space between them, like scattered sand.

From within the mountains, flames burst forth, blazing with fierce intensity and spreading throughout the hells without ceasing; iron spears fall in chaotic profusion to pierce the offenders, and all the spears are ablaze with fire.
At that time, within the northern gate, there were three thousand sinners who raised their voices in loud lamentation and threw themselves to the ground, crying out:
"By what transgression have we now come to enter this place?"
The horse-headed rākṣasa, grasping an iron mace in his hand, struck him on the head and led him into the prison.
In the center of that prison were four great iron dogs, each one yojana in height, with their mouths wide open and fire blazing within them.

When the sinners reach his side, he immediately bellows in rage; hearing this roar, the multitude of sinners are instantly struck with terror and fall to the ground in a swoon, remaining there for a long time.
Blown by hot winds and cut by sharp blades, their bodies are torn asunder; the agony is so excruciating that it is difficult to endure, and they flee toward the various peaks.
Diamond iron mountains spontaneously move and collapse, crushing the sinners, whose bodies instantly dissolve and rot.
The hell-warden yakṣas drive large iron skewers into the ground and impale them; when they call out, "Live! they immediately come back to life.
Thus they undergo myriad forms of bitter and excruciating torment; for one day and one night, they suffer immeasurable retribution, unable to seek life and unable to seek death.
Bao Da asked the Horse-Headed Rākṣasa,
"By what offenses have these sinners come to enter this hell?
The Horse-Headed Rākṣasa replied to the Bodhisattva Bao Da:

"These people are unable to maintain their minds in ascetic practice to seek fields of merit; instead, they rely on their noble lineages and take refuge in official power, using it to manipulate the virtuous and oppress the poor and lowly."
Whether by taking the wealth and treasures of others through wrongful means, or by deceitfully seizing their family estates and livelihoods, they have no sense of shame or remorse.

Because of these causes and conditions, they fall into hell, where for hundreds and thousands of lifetimes there is no prospect of escape. Even if they should later emerge, they will be born in the borderlands among the lowly and base, unable to hear the True Dharma of the Buddha.
Upon hearing this, Baoda wept and departed.

Even if I were to remain in the world for immeasurable eons and speak of the adornments of that Buddha’s great assembly and his land, it would be like a single drop of water from the great ocean.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this Sūtra of the Names of Buddhas, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Bhikṣu Mahānāman, and all the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—along with the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, and all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—were filled with great joy; they received it upon their heads and practiced it accordingly.
"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next perform repentance.

Disciples! Having already repented for the retributions of the three miserable realms and so forth, we shall now, in turn, prostrate with utmost sincerity and repent for the remaining retributions within the human and heavenly realms."

We all receive this lifespan of Jambudvīpa; though it is said to last a hundred years, those who complete it are few indeed. Within that span, those whose prime years end in untimely death are immeasurable in number. There is only the constant oppression of manifold sufferings upon body and mind, such that sorrow, anxiety, fear, and dread never depart for even a moment. All of this is because one’s roots of goodness are weak while evil karma has increased, causing whatever one does in the present to be contrary to one's wishes; know that these are entirely the remaining retributions of evil karma from the past.
Therefore, disciples! Today, with utmost sincerity, we take refuge in the Buddha. Homage to the Buddha Great Adornment of the East. Homage to the Buddha Wisdom Fire of the South.

Homage to the Buddha Supreme Fragrance of Wisdom of the West. Homage to the Buddha King of Wisdom Power of the North. Homage to the Buddha Victorious Deed of Nārāyaṇa of the Southeast. We take refuge in all such Triple Gems throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the realm of empty space.

"Disciples! From beginningless time until this very day, regarding all present and future karmic retributions among humans and devas—including the lingering calamities of past offenses and the retribution for crimes such as physical infirmity, the hundred ailments, and the impairment of the six sense faculties—we repent.
We repent for the retribution for crimes committed in borderlands, through wrong views, and within the three evil realms and eight difficulties."
I repent for the karmic retribution of human beings who suffer from many illnesses, emaciation, and premature death;
I repent for the karmic retribution of human beings whose six types of relatives and kin cannot always protect and sustain one another;
I repent for the karmic retribution of human beings who experience the suffering of separation from loved ones as friends and relatives pass away.
I repent for the retribution of my sins: the sorrow, anxiety, fear, and dread arising from the gathering of human enemies;
the retribution of my sins: the peril, alarm, and terror caused by humans, water, fire, thieves, bandits, and weapons;
the retribution of my sins: the suffering of being solitary, destitute, wandering in exile, scattered abroad, and losing one’s homeland.
I repent for the retribution of my offenses for being bound, confined, and held in human prisons, where I am subjected to flogging and torture;
I repent for the retribution of my offenses for engaging in public or private disputes and litigation, mutually implicating one another and slandering one another;
I repent for the retribution of my offenses for suffering from malignant illnesses that do not subside for years or months, lying prostrate upon my bed unable to rise or move.
Repentance for the karmic retribution of human beings suffering from the cold in winter and pestilence and virulent fevers in summer;
repentance for the karmic retribution of human beings afflicted by malignant winds, swellings, and obstructions;
repentance for the karmic retribution of human beings being sought out by various evil spirits who watch for an opportunity to inflict calamities and misfortunes.
The confession of the retribution for sins committed by humans when birds cry out, or when various monsters, flying corpses, and malevolent ghosts manifest strange and heterodox phenomena;
the confession of the retribution for sins committed by humans when they are injured by tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, or any other evil beasts of water and land;
and the confession of the retribution for sins committed by humans who bind themselves, pierce themselves, commit suicide, or otherwise harm themselves.
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans who, out of their own anxiety, lamentation, self-restraint, anger, and joy, commit transgressions;
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans who throw themselves into pits or leap into fire, or drown or fall from heights;
I repent for the karmic retribution of humans who lack majesty, virtue, fame, or renown.
I repent for the karmic retribution of having clothing and the necessities of life that do not satisfy my heart while in the human realm;
I repent for the karmic retribution of encountering evil associates who create obstacles whenever I move about, enter or exit, or engage in any activity while in the human realm.
Thus, within the realms of humans and devas of the present and future, I repent for immeasurable calamities, untimely deaths, epidemics, misfortunes, afflictions, and the retributions of sin.
Today, with utmost sincerity, before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Holy Assembly, I bare my liver and expose my heart, seeking compassion and repenting.
“May we disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this repentance, in every birth and every life be endowed with perfect physical form,
just like Rāhula; may we always encounter the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, constantly hear the wondrous Dharma,
and have a lifespan equal to heaven and earth, never being entangled by a hundred ailments, and may our six types of close relatives always...”
They shall obtain mutual protection; enemies, bandits, and weapons shall forever depart; garments shall naturally fill their chests and baskets;
bowls shall always be filled with fragrant food of a hundred flavors; prisons and places of confinement shall be transformed into heavenly paradises;
verbal disputes and mutual accusations shall turn into harmony; chronic illnesses shall forever leave the body and mind; and epidemics [shall cease].

May all poisons and calamities be forever removed from the mind; may monsters, goblins, and the like, as well as flying birds, tigers, leopards, jackals, and wolves, and all misfortunes and afflictions of both water and land, depart without exception.

Whether it be the sin of self-mutilation or the sin of harboring anger or joy, I pray that from this moment forth, until the attainment of Buddhahood, such transgressions shall be forever severed and abandoned.

May we, the disciples, not receive retribution in the various evil realms; may we instead give rise to great compassion to rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing them all to fulfill their nature and extensively transform all classes of beings so that they may together ascend to perfect enlightenment.
In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Concerning Retribution for Śramaṇas*, the Jewel-Attainer (Ratnada) entered a Hell of Flaying Skin and Drinking Blood after a short while.
Why is it called the Hell of Flaying Skin and Drinking Blood?

That hell is seventy yojanas in length and breadth; it is surrounded by an iron city with an iron net covering it from above, and from the four gates of the city, boiling iron flows downward, spreading throughout the prison until it is filled with blazing, scorching heat.

Furthermore, there are mechanical crossbows suspended in mid-air; when the sinner strikes against them, they automatically fire at the sinner’s chest. The arrows may enter through the eyes or the mouth, and wherever the arrow strikes, fierce flames break out simultaneously.
At that time, within the southern gate, there were five thousand sinners who wailed and wept loudly, crying out these words:
"By what transgression have we now come to enter this place?"
He rolled about on the ground, refusing to move forward.
A horse-headed rākṣasa, holding an iron hook, aimed it at his face and pulled him into the hell.
Once the sinner had entered, flying flames came to burn his body; his entire frame was scorched and mangled until the skin and flesh were torn apart.

Then there are thousands of varieties of worms that come to drink their blood; they pull at their heads and tear apart their skin and flesh. The yakṣa hell-wardens then hack and flay them amidst this carnage, so that the bones and flesh are scattered in different places, causing ten thousand kinds of excruciating pain.
For one day and one night they undergo immeasurable suffering, dying and being reborn a thousand times, ten thousand times, even through thousands of millions of kalpas,
with no time of release in sight. Bodhidatta asked the Horse-Headed Rākṣasa,
"By what causes and conditions do these sinners undergo such suffering?"

“These sinners received the pure precepts of the Buddha but did not uphold them; their hearts lacked compassion, and with their own hands they flayed living beings and destroyed their Buddha-nature. Because of these sins, they have fallen into this hell.”

If, in the future, they should escape [this state], they will fall among the animals, where for hundreds of thousands of millions of births they will be slaughtered by others; as enemies face one another, there will be no end to it, and if they are born among humans, their faculties will be incomplete.
Upon hearing this, Bodhidatta wept with grief and departed.

with the exception of the four Tathāgatas who have already attained buddhahood within this kalpa.

Having paid homage to the Three Jewels, we next perform repentance. Disciples!..."

I respectfully request the Buddhas of the ten directions, the twelve divisions of the scriptures, all worthy sages, the eight classes of devas and nagas, all sentient beings of the dharma realm, and the assembly gathered here before me to bear witness and know this.
Since beginningless time, the various sins I have committed have been immeasurable and boundless; today, with a sincere heart, I reveal and repent of them, and take refuge in the Buddha.

“Homage to the Buddha Kṣitigarbha-rāja in the eastern direction; homage to the Buddha Paramavikrāmin in the southern direction; homage to the Buddha Anāvaraṇayaśas in the western direction; homage to the Buddha Nāgapuṣpaśrī in the northern direction; homage to the Buddha Anantavaśitabala in the southeastern direction; homage to the Buddha Ratnavaśitā in the southwestern direction; homage to the Buddha Padmavaśitā in the northwestern direction; homage to the Buddha Merudhvaja in the northeastern direction; homage to the Buddha Pratiṣṭhitavīrya in the downward direction; homage to the Buddha Vaiḍūryaprabhā-samṛddha in the upward direction. I take refuge in all such Triple Gems throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space in the ten directions.”

"Disciples! From beginningless kalpas until this present body, you have killed all members of the Triple Gem, teachers, the Sangha, parents, six types of relatives, spiritual friends, and sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm; the number is beyond reckoning.

You have stolen all property belonging to the Triple Gem, teachers, the Sangha, parents, six types of relatives, spiritual friends, and sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm; the number is beyond reckoning."

They gave rise to perverse thoughts toward all the Triple Gem, teachers, the Saṃgha, parents, the six classes of kinsmen, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, in incalculable numbers;

they uttered false speech to deceive and mislead all the Triple Gem, teachers, the Saṃgha, parents, the six classes of kinsmen, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, in incalculable numbers;

and they engaged in frivolous speech to mock and toy with all the Triple Gem, teachers, the Saṃgha, parents, the six classes of kinsmen, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, in incalculable numbers.

They have used harsh speech to insult, revile, slander, and disparage all the Three Jewels, teachers, the Saṃgha, parents, the six classes of kinsmen, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, in numbers beyond measure.

They have engaged in double-tongued speech to incite strife and cause division among all the Three Jewels, teachers, the Saṃgha, parents, the six classes of kinsmen, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, in numbers beyond measure.

Or they have violated the five precepts, the eight precepts, the ten precepts, the ten virtuous precepts, the two hundred and fifty precepts, the five hundred precepts, the Bodhisattva’s three clusters of precepts, the ten inexhaustible precepts, and even all other precepts and codes of dignified conduct; they have committed these acts themselves, taught others to do so, or rejoiced upon seeing them done, in numbers beyond measure.

"These various transgressions are as numerous as the infinite atoms of the great earth throughout the ten directions; our committed sins are likewise infinite and innumerable. As space is infinite, our committed sins are also infinite; as skillful means are infinite, our committed sins are also infinite; as the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is infinite, our committed sins are also infinite; as the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is infinite, our committed sins are also infinite. As sentient beings are infinite, our acts of plundering and killing them are also infinite; as the Triple Gem is infinite, our acts of violating and damaging it are also infinite; and as the categories of precepts are infinite, our acts of breaking and transgressing them are also infinite."

Such offenses as these cannot be known by those above, the various Bodhisattvas, nor by those below, the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; only a Buddha and a Buddha can know the extent of my transgressions.

Now, before the Triple Gem and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, I openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal my faults; I only pray that the Triple Gem and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm throughout the ten directions will hear my confession.

"Disciples! From beginningless kalpas until now, all manner of evils have been committed; by these causes and conditions, great sorrow and suffering have arisen. There has been poverty, destitution, anxiety, distress, and alarm; through fear of evil karma, the mind is constantly timid and inferior, finding no moment of joy anywhere."

The World-Honored Ones of Great Compassion currently dwelling in the ten directions, who are able to eliminate all fears of sentient beings: we pray that you will accept our sincere repentance. We now repent for all past evils and sincerely confess our present actions.

Regarding those deeds not yet committed, I dare not commit them henceforth; regarding those already committed, I dare not conceal them. I now repent for all actions of the three types of body, the four types of speech, and the three types of mind.
The perils of birth and death, the various difficulties of lustful desires, and the hardships of deluded afflictions—all such perils as these, I now repent.

The difficulty of a fickle and restless mind, the difficulty of associating with evil friends, the perils of the three realms of existence, and the perils of the three poisons; the difficulty of encountering no calamities, the difficulty of meeting a favorable time, the difficulty of cultivating merit, and the difficulty of meeting a Buddha.
We now repent for all such difficulties.
Disciples! We now, on behalf of all sentient beings and for our own selves, take refuge and repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions.

Throughout immeasurable kalpas, all sentient beings have failed to recognize the Buddhas or the kindness of their parents; they do not understand wholesome dharmas and instead commit manifold evils. Relying on their own lineage and various riches, they indulge in negligence during their prime years, performing all manner of unwholesome deeds. Their minds dwell on what is not good and their mouths commit evil karma; following whatever they create with their minds, they fail to see their own transgressions.

Ordinary worldlings act with folly, shrouded in the darkness of ignorance; they associate with evil friends, their minds distracted by afflictions. Due to the conditions of the five desires, anger arises in their hearts; lacking contentment, they commit various evils. Associating with those who are not noble, they give rise to stinginess and jealousy; due to the conditions of poverty, they act with deceit and craftiness to do evil. Bound to others, they are constantly filled with fear; lacking self-mastery, they create all manner of evils. Greed, hatred, and delusion agitate their minds; driven by thirsting craving, they perform various evils. Dependent on clothing, food, and women, they suffer from the burning heat of various fetters and afflictions; they become attached to other men, their hearts stained by passion.

Or, regarding oxen, horses, donkeys, mules, sheep, and all other species of birds and beasts, one may give rise to thoughts of them as women; failing to rely on the practice of the Buddha, one commits various evils through the three karmas accumulated by body, speech, and mind—all such immeasurable and boundless transgressions, we now repent in their entirety.
"Disciples! From time immemorial until this very day, we may have failed to show reverence to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Noble Sangha; all such transgressions, we now fully repent."
Or failing to show respect toward pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas—all such transgressions, I now repent in their entirety.

Out of ignorance, I slandered the True Dharma; I failed to know how to revere my parents and elders; I was shrouded by delusion, prideful and negligent; and driven by greed, hatred, and delusion, I committed various evils—all such transgressions, I now repent in their entirety.

I took pleasure in drinking alcohol without knowing moderation or limit; I gave wine to the assembly of monks, to those who uphold the precepts, to bhikṣuṇīs, to those who have extinguished their worldly thoughts, or to those in meditative concentration. Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless; today I direct my mind toward them and take refuge in repentance.

“May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession, vow that in every birth and every life we shall forever abandon the form of the womb. May we, according to our aspirations, attain rebirth and obtain the power of the six supernormal knowledges (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) to rescue and gather all suffering beings. As far as the reaches of space and the *dharmadhātu*, may my vows likewise extend. For all sentient beings in the hells and among the hungry ghosts who are impoverished, distressed, and oppressed by various sufferings and afflictions—may all such sufferings as these be completely extinguished.”

may the disciple, by virtue of the merit accomplished through this repentance, depart from birth and death to reach the shore of great wisdom; may they turn the unsurpassed wheel, which is subtle and pure, and may all their aspirations and requests be fully realized and perfected.

Furthermore, may the blind gain sight, the deaf gain hearing, the mute be able to speak, and the naked obtain clothing. May those who are impoverished and destitute find treasure-troves, their granaries and storehouses overflowing so that they lack for nothing; may all receive peace, security, and happiness, until not even a single person suffers.

Furthermore, may all sentient beings face one another with hearts of loving-kindness and gaze upon each other with the Buddha-eye; may their physical forms be upright and majestic, pleasing to behold by others, and may their bodies be adorned with supreme and wondrous features, serving as true spiritual friends to the retinue of Bodhi.

In the *Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions and Answers Regarding Retribution for Śramaṇas*, the Jewel-Attainer (Ratnada) entered a hell called "Flying Fire Screaming and Splitting Heads" shortly thereafter.

This hell was sixty yojanas in length and breadth; it was surrounded by iron walls with an iron net covering it above. Within it, iron spikes were as sharp as the points of awls, and a fierce wind blew fire whose smoke and flames blazed forth to burn the sinners.
At that time, among those at the eastern gate, thirty-six thousand offenders cried out these words:
"For what sin have we now come to this place?"

The horse-headed rākṣasa grasps an iron club in his hand and strikes toward the back; the sinner steps forward and is kicked by foot. The sinner stumbles and falls with every step, pierced by descending iron spikes and scorched by flying flames that blaze from the eyes or issue from the mouth.
The sinners cry out and flee hither and thither; they wish to run east, but flying flames burn against them from behind, and they wish to gallop west, yet the fire returns to scorch their faces.

The horse-headed rākṣasas seize the sinners by the hair with their hands and tear them apart, so that their skin and fur fall away and their bones are shattered to pieces. Then hungry dogs come to devour their flesh, and hungry ghosts come to drink their blood.

For one day and one night, they undergo myriad forms of suffering; they seek life but cannot find it, and they seek death but cannot find it. They undergo retribution for thousands of millions of kalpas without reaching its end, and even after escaping that state, they will constantly be reborn as animals.
Bao Da asked the horse-headed rākṣasa,
"By what offenses did these people cause themselves to enter here?

"These sinners, having received the Buddha’s prohibitive precepts yet failing to uphold them, pluck the feathers and fur of birds and beasts, injuring all species without a thought of compassion; those who are thus captured have their spirits soaring and their souls fleeing in terror, unable to endure the piercing pain, which is so agonizing as to be unbearable."

Yet these people pluck out their feathers until they are raw and ruined, regarding it as pleasure; they possess no compassion and no sense of shame. Because of these transgressions, they fall into this hell.
Upon hearing this, Bodhisattva Baoda wept with grief and departed.
