Homage to the Buddha Loushi. "The names of the Buddhas who appear in this Bhadrakalpa are as follows.
If a person hears the names of these thousand Buddhas, they will not fear error or confusion and will certainly attain nirvana."

All those who possess wisdom, upon hearing the names of the Buddhas, should with single-mindedness refrain from negligence and practice with diligent vigor. Lest they lose this opportunity and fall back into the evil realms to undergo various sufferings, they should abide securely in the observance of the precepts, cultivate extensive learning as appropriate, and never be separated from the perfection of profound patience; such a person shall be able to encounter a thousand Buddhas.

"If one holds and recites these names of the thousand Buddhas, then the multitude of sins accumulated over immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas will be extinguished. One shall certainly attain the various samādhis, supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), and unimpeded wisdom of the Buddhas, as well as all dharma-gates and dhāraṇīs. All sūtras and the various forms of wisdom for preaching the Dharma according to what is appropriate—all these should be sought from within this samādhi."

When practicing this samādhi, one should maintain a pure livelihood and refrain from deception; remaining free from fame and profit, one should not harbor envy and should practice the six points of reverent harmony. One who practices in this manner will swiftly attain the dharma of samādhi.
"Next, pay homage to the Great Dharma Wheel of the Tripitaka, the Honored Scriptures of the Twelve Divisions.
Homage to all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the ten directions.
We take refuge in such immeasurable and boundless great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions."
“Homage to all such bodhisattvas; may they all remember me, and I shall reverently pay homage and seek the stage of avaivartika.
I pay homage to the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all worthy sages.”
"I take refuge in these immeasurable and boundless Pratyekabuddhas.
Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next perform repentance:

Having finished repenting for all retributions, we shall now once again collectively repent for all transgressions and earnestly entreat the Buddhas of the ten directions to provide protection and deliverance.

Since beginningless, immeasurable hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions, and billions of kalpas, the evil karma we have created cannot be fully described—whether it be the commission of the ten unwholesome paths, the five heinous crimes, or the slandering of the Vaipulya sutras; or whether it be the creation of immeasurable, asankhyeya offenses—we now take refuge in the Buddhas of the ten directions, take refuge in the Dharma of the ten directions, and take refuge in the Sangha of the ten directions.

"Next, I again take refuge and prostrate to Akṣobhya Buddha of the east, Ratnaśrī Buddha of the south, Amitābha Buddha of the west, Supuṣpacandra Buddha of the north, Gandhottama Tathāgata of the zenith, and Koṭirūpa Buddha of the nadir; I prostrate to the Great Being Samantabhadra of the east, Lokadhara Great Being of the south, Avalokiteśvara Great Being of the west, Pūrṇacandra Great Being of the north, Gaganagañja Great Being of the zenith, and Dṛḍhaśila Great Being of the nadir; to our original teacher Śākyamuni Buddha, and I take refuge in the buddha-nature of future buddhas."

“Furthermore, I prostrate to the transformation Buddhas and Great Beings in other directions, such as Vimalakīrti and Mañjuśrī; I also prostrate to the holy ones who appear on the four paths, such as Ānanda and Kāśyapa; and I likewise take refuge in those at the initial stage of the teaching.”
"I prostrate before the Great Treasury of the twelve divisions of the sutras, as well as other scriptures, the Vaipulya and orthodox canons, and the eightfold relics and images.

I also take refuge in the Four Heavenly Kings who currently perform Buddha-works; the Śakras and Brahmās of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven with its thirty-three devas; and all the seers and immortals—whether in the heavens, upon the earth, or beneath it, or in the mountains, forests, and under trees—who possess great supernormal powers, the divine eye, and the divine ear. I pray that you will grant me your hearing and knowledge to serve as witnesses for all. I pray that all sentient beings who have not yet repented may, upon performing this repentance, all attain the eradication of their transgressions."
Disciple! Today, in repentance, I strip away my very heart and expose my innermost soul, taking refuge in the Buddha with utmost sincerity.

Homage to the Buddha Victorious Mind in the East. Homage to the Buddha Victorious Sage in the South. Homage to the Buddha Sound Mountain in the West. Homage to the Buddha Victorious Radiance in the North. Homage to the Buddha Loving Purity in the Southeast. Homage to the Buddha Destroyer of All Terrors in the Southwest. Homage to the Buddha Fearless Skillful Transformation in the Northwest. Homage to the Buddha King of Supreme Reflected Light in the Northeast. Homage to the Buddha King of Encountering Supernatural Powers in the Nadir. Homage to the Buddha King of Abundant Lotus Honor in the Zenith. I take refuge in all such Triple Gems throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the reaches of empty space.

“Disciples! From time immemorial throughout the beginningless world until now, this evil body has been deluded and the mind distracted; the immeasurable inverted views, afflictions, and evil karmas cannot be fully recounted. We have committed manifold transgressions without realizing them ourselves. Our evil minds blaze fiercely as we fail to perceive future lives, seeing only the present and habitually indulging in afflictions while distancing ourselves from roots of goodness. Obstructed by evil karma, we draw near to unwholesome associates.”
Or one may commit an unrighteous act toward a bhikṣu, an unrighteous act toward a bhikṣuṇī, an unrighteous act toward one's parents, or again, an unrighteous act before the great assembly.

Or again, they may willfully misappropriate the property of the Saṃgha, or act with partiality toward the five divisions of the Saṃgha, or engage in such improper conduct, or speak of the immeasurable evil fruits of the world.

They may kill sentient beings who possess the roots of merit for enlightenment, or they may slander the Dharma masters, declaring what is Dharma to be non-Dharma and what is non-Dharma to be Dharma; they claim that the Tathāgata is impermanent, the True Dharma is impermanent, and the Sangha Jewel is impermanent; they take no pleasure in giving and instead believe and accept false teachings.
Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless.

Therefore, today, with immeasurable fear and immeasurable shame and remorse, we take refuge in the Triple Gem—the Buddhas, whose compassion is like that of parents toward their children, and the Bodhisattvas who are our spiritual friends—and we request your permission to now openly confess and repent.

"Disciples! Since immeasurable kalpas past, you have committed the five heinous crimes, or violated the prohibitions and precepts of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present; you have acted as icchantikas, uttering coarse words to slander the True Dharma, and having created such grave karma, you have never repented or reformed, nor do you possess a sense of shame or remorse."

Or perhaps they have committed the ten evil deeds and other such offenses; knowing for themselves that they have certainly committed such grave matters, yet from the beginning their hearts were devoid of fear or shame, and they silently accepted offerings without ever confessing them.
Regarding that True Dharma, they lacked any intention to protect, cherish, or establish it; meanwhile, they disparaged and despised it, speaking with many faults and evils.
Some even claimed that the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha do not exist, or else they did not believe in the existence of the various hells where retribution is received.

Such transgressions as these are immeasurable and boundless; today, with immeasurable fear and immeasurable shame and remorse, we take refuge in the Triple Gem, the compassionate Buddhas, the Vaipulya sutras, our parents, the Bodhisattvas, and our spiritual friends, and request that you grant us permission to openly confess and repent.

"Disciples! From immeasurable kalpas past until this very day, you have sometimes held the four inverted views; you have spoken of the four grave offenses as *sthūlātyaya*, and spoken of *sthūlātyaya* offenses as the four grave offenses; you have declared what was an offense to be no offense, and what was not an offense to be an offense; you have called a light sin heavy, and a heavy sin light; you have viewed the pure as impure, and the impure as pure."

Furthermore, those with wrong views may praise worldly treatises and show no respect for the Buddha’s sutras; they engage in various evil discourses, keep the eight impure things, take what is truly the Buddha’s word to be the Mara’s word, and take what is truly the Mara’s word to be the Buddha’s word.

Alternatively, some may believe and accept what the six heretical teachers have said, or they may say: "The Tathāgata has today entered parinirvāṇa; the Three Jewels are impermanent. Thus, their bodies and minds give rise to delusions and immeasurable inverted views.

Therefore, today, with immeasurable fear and immeasurable shame and remorse, we take refuge in the Triple Gem—the Buddhas, whose compassion is like that of parents, the Vaipulya sutras, and the Bodhisattvas who are our spiritual friends—and request that you grant us permission to openly confess and repent.

"May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this repentance, in every birth and throughout all lifetimes, deliver and rescue all sentient beings of the ten directions; may they distance themselves from the ten unwholesome actions and practice the ten wholesome actions; may all who suffer find peace and stability, and may inconceivable asankhyeya multitudes be established in the ten stages."
Whatever wholesome dharmas exist in this land and in all other worlds, I dedicate them all.
Through the merit of my cultivation of goodness in body, speech, and mind, may I realize the Unsurpassed Way in a future life.
May all women become men, endowed with wisdom and diligent without slackening; may they all practice the path of the Bodhisattva, cultivating and accumulating the six pāramitās with a devoted mind.

Whatever various kinds of virtuous and sublime merits have been performed by all sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa and in immeasurable worlds in other directions, I now rejoice in them with a profound heart.

By means of these merits of sympathetic joy and the wholesome karma performed through my body, speech, and mind, I vow that in future lives I shall attain the Unsurpassed Way and obtain the pure, stainless, and auspicious fruits of retribution, fully realizing the perfect enlightenment of a Tathāgata.
In the *Mahāyāna Padma-ratna-bodhi-praśna-vyākaraṇa-sādhūpāya-śramaṇa-sūtra*, the horse-headed rākṣasa said to Bodhisattva Ratnabodhi:
"Furthermore, these hells are immeasurable in number."
If there is a bhikṣu who, with impure boots or shoes, treads upon the pure incense chamber of the Vaipulya Mahāyāna, he shall fall into the Iron Spiked Hell (Ayaḥśalmalī-niraya).

If there is a bhikṣu who, harboring anger in his heart, raises his hand toward the Teacher even for a single thought of evil, he shall fall into the Hell of Burning Hands and Feet (Jvalita-hastapāda-niraya).
If there is a bhikṣu who raises his voice to revile his teacher with even a single evil word, he shall fall into the Copper Dog Hell.
If there is a bhikṣu whose heart lacks compassion and who boils the flesh of sentient beings in a cauldron, he shall enter the Iron Mountain Hell.
The horse-headed rākṣasa said to Bodhisattva Baoda, "Such retributions for sin are all not in vain.
Baoda wept with grief and returned to the Maṇḍala of Magadha; he circumambulated the Buddha seven times and spoke while weeping:
"In this eastern region between the Iron Ring Mountains, there are immeasurable hells; how shall I deliver these various sinners?

"Create a divine transformation and enter therein; call out to all the sinners so that they may all emerge, and let the sufferings of hell all find rest. Let them all come to see me, and I shall preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the Way."

At that time, Precious Arrival (Ratnapāṇi) immediately manifested his supernatural powers and went to the hells; sitting upon a high dais, he called out to the various sinners and the Asura Kings: "You sinners!"

The Honored One among men in the three realms has appeared in the world; his great compassion shines universally so that none fail to receive benefit, and he causes them to emerge from the three realms.
Upon hearing these words, King Asura gave rise to a heart of joy and called out to the sinners:
"I am now as joyful as a prisoner who has received a pardon, or like one returning to life after death.

When these sinners were brought before Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, the places of suffering in hell were all transformed into states of joy. They then proceeded to the Buddha’s abode, where the Buddha preached the Dharma for them, and they all attained realization of the Way."

When this chapter was preached, twenty thousand bhikṣus attained the path of arhatship; five thousand bhikṣuṇīs attained the fruit of srotāpanna; six thousand princes attained the purity of the Dharma-eye; and eight hundred women attained the mind of the third dhyāna. The devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits all departed filled with joy.
The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Teaching on the Retribution of Sinful Karma and the Instruction of the Hells. Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a retinue of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and śrāvakas.
Bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, as well as devas, nāgas, spirits, and others, all assembled there.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Present now are various kinds of beings—those in the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, slaves, the poor, the wealthy, the noble, and the lowly. I only pray that the World-Honored One will fully expound upon them."

Whenever sentient beings hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, it is like a child finding its mother, like a sick person finding a physician, like a naked person finding clothing, or like one in darkness finding a lamp; the World-Honored One’s preaching of the Dharma for the benefit of sentient beings is likewise so.

At that time, the World-Honored One, observing that the moment had arrived and knowing the earnest entreaties of the bodhisattvas, emitted a light from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows that illuminated the world; the sufferings of the hells were stilled, and all became peaceful.

At that time, all sentient beings undergoing retribution for their offenses, following the Buddha’s radiance, came to where the Buddha was, circumambulated him seven times, and paid homage with a sincere heart.
They entreated the World-Honored One to expound and guide them, so that these sentient beings might obtain liberation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa, acting as an instigator for the sake of all sentient beings, addressed the Buddha, saying:

At that time, sentient beings are hacked, pounded, and beheaded by the hell-wardens. They are cut from their feet up to their crowns; once they have been completely severed, a skillful wind blows them back to life, only for them to be beheaded again."

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, this person failed to believe in the Triple Gem and was unfilial toward his parents; he was a butcher and executioner who slaughtered and harmed sentient beings, and thus he incurred this retribution."

“Furthermore, there are sentient beings whose bodies are numb and paralyzed, whose eyebrows and beards fall out, and whose entire bodies are festering so severely that birds nest and deer lie within them.
Human tracks have ceased, and they defile their own kin; people do not even look upon them with pleasure, and this disease is called leprosy.”
"What offense led to this? The Buddha said, "In a previous life, because you did not believe in the Triple Gem,

were unfilial toward your parents, destroyed stupas and monasteries, stripped the robes from practitioners of the Way, struck and shot sages and holy ones, harmed your teachers and elders, constantly failed to repay kindness and turned your back on benevolence and righteousness, habitually engaged in the lustful excesses of pigs and dogs toward those you should revere, and showed no sense of shame regardless of kinship or distance, you have incurred this retribution."

“Furthermore, there are sentient beings whose bodies are large and tall, yet they are deaf, dull-witted, and footless, crawling on their bellies as they move about. They subsist solely by eating earth and mud to sustain their lives, while being bitten and eaten by various small insects; they constantly undergo such unbearable suffering that it is impossible to endure.”

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, he acted according to his own will as a human being; he did not believe in kind words or virtuous speech, was unfilial toward his parents, and was rebellious toward the sovereign of the time."

If one serves as an emperor, a high minister, a regional commander, a provincial governor, a district magistrate, or a palace guard, yet relies on their power and influence to plunder the property of the people without justification, causing them to fall into poverty and suffering, they shall therefore incur this retribution.
"Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are blind in both eyes and see nothing; they may brush against trees or fall into ditches and pits.
When they die and subsequently receive another body, it is likewise so."
"By what offense was this caused? The Buddha said, "In a previous life,

because you sat in disbelief regarding the retribution of sin and merit, obstructed the light of the Buddhas, sewed the eyes of hawks shut, confined sentient beings in cages, and stuffed their heads into leather bags so they could not see, you have incurred this retribution."
"Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are gluttonous, mute, and unable to speak; if they have something to say, they cannot express it clearly.
By what offense is this caused?"
The Buddha said, "In a previous life,

because you sat idly slandering the Triple Gem, disparaging the Noble Path, discussing the faults and merits of others while seeking out their shortcomings, and falsely accusing the virtuous while harboring malice toward the worthy, you have incurred this retribution."
“Furthermore, there are sentient beings whose bellies are large and their necks are thin, such that they cannot swallow food; if they do eat anything, it turns into pus and blood.

"In a previous life, he stole food belonging to the Sangha; or when a great assembly was provided with delicacies, he took sesame and rice in secret and ate them himself. He was stingy with his own possessions and craved only what was his own.
He constantly harbored evil intentions and gave others poisonous drugs that caused their breath to cease. For these reasons, he has incurred this retribution."

“Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are constantly pierced through their hundred joints by the wardens of hell with glowing iron nails; once they have been finished with the needles, fire spontaneously arises and incinerates their bodies until they are completely scorched and rotten.”

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, while serving as a barber, you injured people's bodies and were unable to cure their ailments; you deceived others to take their property and caused them needless suffering. For these reasons, you have incurred this retribution."

“Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are constantly kept in cauldrons by the ox-headed Apsaras, who seize them with iron forks, drag them into the cauldrons to boil them until they are烂 (làn—putrid/softened), and then blow upon them to restore them to life so that they may be boiled again.”
The Buddha said, "In a previous life, you slaughtered sentient beings, pouring boiling water over them until their hair fell out; because this was beyond measure, you have incurred this retribution."

"Furthermore, there are sentient beings in a great city where hot ashes reach up to their hearts; though the four gates are open, they close as soon as one arrives. Running hither and thither, they cannot escape and are utterly consumed by the flames."

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, you burned mountains and marshes and breached the dikes of ponds and lakes, causing various sentient beings to drown and die; therefore, you have incurred this retribution."
“Furthermore, there are sentient beings who constantly dwell amidst the Snowy Mountains, their skin and flesh flayed by the cold winds.
By what offense is this brought about?

"In a previous life, I was a highway robber who stripped people of their clothing; during the bitter cold of winter, I caused others to die of frostbite, and I flayed oxen and sheep until their suffering was unbearable; therefore, I have incurred this retribution."

“Furthermore, there are sentient beings who constantly dwell atop mountains of knives and trees of swords; whenever they grasp anything, their limbs and joints are immediately wounded, sliced, severed, and destroyed.
By what offense is this brought about?”

"In a previous life, he made his livelihood by slaughtering and cooking sentient beings. With knives he cut, flayed, and pierced them until their bones and flesh were separated and their heads and feet scattered; he hung them on high racks to weigh and sell them, or else hung them alive in unbearable agony. Therefore, he has incurred this retribution."
“Furthermore, there are sentient beings who lack one or more of the five faculties.
By what offense is this brought about?

"In a previous life, I pursued flying hawks and running dogs, shooting at birds and beasts; I either split their heads or severed their legs, destroying their heads and wings while they were alive, and thus I have incurred this retribution."
"Furthermore, there are sentient beings who suffer from chronic ailments, backaches, and stiffness in their waists and hips; they have clubfoot or broken hands and are unable to walk.

"In a previous life, when he was a human being, he was a malicious executioner who traveled about with his weapons leveled; moreover, he repeatedly caused people to fall into pits and traps before and after performing his deeds. For these reasons, he has incurred this retribution."
“Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are prone to anger, delusion, madness, or stupidity, unable to distinguish between the beautiful and the ugly.

"In a previous life, while intoxicated and deranged by drinking alcohol, I committed thirty-six transgressions; subsequently, I obtained this deluded body like that of a drunkard, unable to distinguish between the honorable and the lowly, and thus incurred this retribution."
Those who delight in bows, swords, and riding become barbarians;
those who delight in killing and hunting become jackals and wolves;
those who delight in wearing flowered headdresses while entering monasteries become horned insects in their subsequent lives.
Those who take pleasure in wearing long skirts will later become long-tailed insects;
those who delight in harsh speech will later become dogs;
and those who speak ill of others with slanderous stings and are full of anger will later become snakes and vipers.
"One who delights in foul sounds will later become an owl or a screech-owl;
one who rejoices in words of calamity will later become a wild fox.
“[The Buddha] saw a being with a massive body, its entire surface devoid of skin, its form like a lump of flesh, traveling through the air.
The Buddha said, “In the past, it fell from its own womb and subsequently fell into hell; therefore, it undergoes this suffering.”
"I see a sentient being whose entire body is without skin, consisting of nothing but a single mass of flesh, traveling through the air while crows and hawks follow and peck at it."
The Buddha said, "In a past life, he was a butcher; having already fallen into hell, he still undergoes this suffering.

“[The Buddha] saw a sentient being whose body was bound by a net of copper and iron; fire constantly blazed, burning his very frame as he traveled through the air. The Buddha said, “In a past life, he was a fisherman;
due to the remaining retribution from that time in hell, he now receives this body. This is likewise true for those who used nets to catch birds or nets to catch rabbits.”

"I saw a being of immense body who was headless, with eyes growing on both sides and a mouth in its chest; its body constantly flowed with blood, and various insects devoured it, causing pain that pierced to the very marrow of its bones."
"In a past life, he delighted in severing the heads of insects and beasts; having already suffered in hell for that, he has now obtained this body.
[He] saw a being with a single massive body, whose entire frame was covered in hair as sharp as knives; these hairs were ablaze with fire, cutting and burning his body.
The Buddha said, "In a previous life, he took the lives of all beings with swords and blades; this suffering is the continued retribution for that karma in hell."

*The Scripture of the Names of Buddhas*, Fascicle 30. *The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Names of Buddhas*: "Next, pay homage to the Great Dharma-Wheel of the Treasury of the Honored Scriptures of the Twelve Divisions.
Homage to the *Maitreya-vyākaraṇa Sūtra* (The Scripture on Maitreya’s Descent to Be Born)."
Homage to the Sutra of the Dragon King of the Ocean;
homage to the Sutra of Increasing Merit;
homage to the Sutra of the Bodhisattva in the Womb.
Homage to the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*. Next, pay homage to the great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Constantly Smiling Tranquil Root;
homage to the Bodhisattva Superior Path of the Padma;
homage to the Bodhisattva Vast Thought.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Abiding in All Compassionate Vision.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Who Severs All Evil Dharmas.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Abiding in All Sounds.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Flower Adornment;
homage to the Bodhisattva Moonlight Radiance;
homage to the Bodhisattva Supreme Intention.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Pure Intention. [Homage] to the one thousand four hundred Buddhas above this, to the twelve divisions of the scriptures, and to all worthy ones and sages.

Homage to the Bodhisattva Vajramati; homage to the Bodhisattva Vardhamānamati; homage to the Bodhisattva Susthitamati; homage to the Bodhisattva Sunetra; homage to the Bodhisattva Padmagarbha; homage to the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīśvararāja; homage to the Bodhisattva Samantacārin; homage to the Bodhisattva Bodhiprabhāsa. I take refuge in these and all other immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas of the ten directions.
"Next, pay homage to all the worthy sages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas:

*Namo* to the Real Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Incomparable Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Joyful Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Delighting Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Rejoicing Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the twelve Brahmā-pratyekabuddhas; *Namo* to the ten Pratyekabuddhas named Brahmā; *Namo* to the Fire-body Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Equal-Enlightenment Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Mahānāman Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Mind-above Pratyekabuddha; *Namo* to the Pure-Hair Pratyekabuddha. I take refuge in these and all other immeasurable and boundless Pratyekabuddhas."
"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next proceed to repentance.

O assembly, since our bodies and minds are now tranquil, free from flattery and hindrances, this is precisely the time to give rise to goodness and extinguish evil. Furthermore, each of you should individually initiate four types of contemplative practices as the preliminary means for the eradication of transgressions."
Third, one contemplates one's own body;
fourth, one contemplates the body of the Tathāgata.

Regarding the first contemplation of causes and conditions: one knows that these transgressions of mine arise from ignorance, from unwholesome reflection and a lack of the power of right observation. Failing to recognize their faults, I have distanced myself from virtuous friends—the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas—and have followed the path of Māra along treacherous and deviant ways. Like a fish swallowing a hook without knowing its peril, like a silkworm spinning a cocoon to entangle and bind itself, or like a goose rushing into fire to burn and rot itself, by these causes and conditions I am unable to escape on my own.

"Second, regarding the contemplation of retribution: all evil and unwholesome karmas result in the endless fruits of suffering as one transmigrates through the three periods of time; one sinks into the vast ocean of the great night of boundlessness, devoured by the rākṣasas of the afflictions, with future births and deaths shrouded in darkness without limit."

Even if one were to receive the retribution of becoming a Wheel-Turning Sage King—ruling over the four continents with sovereign flight and possessing the seven treasures—after the end of that life, one cannot avoid the evil realms. Once the fruit of the four formless attainments, the highest honor within the three realms, is exhausted, one returns to become a worm on an ox's hump; how much more so for those of lesser merit?

Those who lack merit and are furthermore indolent, failing to diligently practice repentance, are like those who embrace a stone and sink into a deep abyss; it is extremely difficult for them to seek deliverance.

"Third, I observe my own self: although I possess the true cause—the nature of numinous awakening—it is shrouded by the dense forest of the darkness of afflictions; lacking the power of the enabling cause, it cannot be made manifest."

I should now arouse the supreme mind to shatter the heavy obstacles of ignorance and perversion, sever the causes of the false suffering of birth and death, manifest the great, luminous wisdom of the Tathāgata, and establish the wondrous fruit of unsurpassed nirvāṇa.

"Fourth, one contemplates the body of the Tathāgata as unconditioned, tranquil, and luminous, transcending the four propositions and severing the hundred negations; it is replete with all virtues, profound and eternally abiding. Although he enters parinirvāṇa through skillful means, his compassionate rescue and reception of beings have never for a moment ceased."
To give rise to such a mind may be called an excellent ford for extinguishing transgressions and an essential practice for removing obstacles.
Today, with utmost sincerity, we take refuge in the Buddha.

“Homage to the Buddha Victorious Treasury of Jewel Light in the east; homage to the Buddha Jewel Accumulation Manifestation in the south; homage to the Buddha Dharma-realm Wisdom Lamp in the west; homage to the Buddha Supreme Subduer in the north; homage to the Buddha Dragon Sovereign King in the southeast; homage to the Buddha Turning All Birth and Death in the southwest; homage to the Buddha Infinite Wisdom Sovereign in the northwest; homage to the Buddha Infinite Virtue Moon in the northeast; homage to the Buddha Ocean Wisdom Supernatural Power in the nadir; homage to the Buddha All-Victorious King in the zenith. Thus [I take refuge] in all the Triple Gems throughout the entirety of space in the ten directions.”

"Disciples! From time immemorial until this very day, you have nurtured afflictions that have grown ever deeper, ever thicker, ever more abundant, and ever more rampant. These afflictions shroud the eye of wisdom so that nothing may be seen, severing all roots of goodness so that they cannot continue."

The arising of hindrances prevents one from seeing the Buddha, hearing the True Dharma, or meeting the Noble Sangha. The hindrance of afflictions (*kleśāvaraṇa*) consists of: the hindrance of not seeing all past and future wholesome and unwholesome karmic actions;
the hindrance of afflictions regarding receiving the status of humans, devas, or those of noble rank;
and the hindrance of afflictions regarding the meditative bliss and merit of birth in the realms of form and formlessness.

The afflictive hindrance of being unable to attain sovereign supernormal powers—such as flying, appearing and disappearing, and being born everywhere in the pure lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions to hear the Dharma;
the afflictive hindrances encountered when practicing the meditation on counting the breath (*ānāpāna*) and the contemplation of impurity (*aśubha-bhāvanā*);
and the afflictive hindrances encountered when practicing the meditations on loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity (*maitrī-karuṇā-muditopekṣā*).
Studying the meaning of the seven expedient means and the three contemplations constitutes an afflictive hindrance;
studying the four foundations of mindfulness, the stages of heat, summits, and patience constitutes an afflictive hindrance;
and studying the dharma of hearing, reflection, cultivation, and the supreme mundane dharma constitutes an afflictive hindrance.
One studies the Middle Way of the equality of emptiness to resolve the afflictive hindrances;
one studies mindfulness of the path to resolve the afflictive hindrances of manifesting signs;
and one studies the seven factors of enlightenment to resolve the afflictive hindrances of non-manifestation.
One studies the affliction-obstructions regarding the contemplation of the causal conditions of the factors of enlightenment;
one studies the affliction-obstructions regarding the eight liberations and the nine emptinesses;
and one studies the affliction-obstructions regarding the ten knowledges and the three samādhis.
The afflictive hindrance to studying the three knowledges, the six supernormal powers, and the four analytical insights;
the afflictive hindrance to studying the six perfections and the four immeasurables;
and the afflictive hindrance to studying the four means of attraction for the sake of extensive transformation.
The afflictive hindrances to learning the four great vows of the Mahāyāna mind;
the afflictive hindrances to learning the ten clarities and the ten practices;
and the afflictive hindrances to learning the ten dedications and the ten vows.
The afflictive obstacles of clear understanding on the first, second, third, and fourth stages;
the afflictive obstacles regarding various knowledge and views on the fifth, sixth, and seventh stages;
and the afflictive obstacles regarding the dual illumination of training on the eighth, ninth, and tenth stages.
In this way, up to the superior afflictions that obstruct the millions of asaṃkhyeyas of practices for attaining the fruit of Buddhahood—
such obstructions to practice are immeasurable and boundless,

"Today, having arrived here, I prostrate with utmost sincerity before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Assembly of Sages, and I repent with shame and remorse, praying that all [obstacles] may be extinguished.

'I pray that by means of this repentance, all afflictions that obstruct various practices shall be removed; may I, as a disciple, be born freely in every place, not being turned back by the karma of fetters. Through the supernormal power of *ṛddhi*, may I reach all pure Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions in a single thought-moment to gather in and transform sentient beings.'"

Regarding the profound realms of all meditative concentrations and the unimpeded penetration of all knowledge and vision, his mind is able to universally accord with all phenomena; he delights in inexhaustible exposition without becoming stained or attached. Having attained mastery over the mind and mastery over the Dharma, he possesses mastery over wisdom and mastery over skillful means. He brings about the ultimate and permanent severance of these afflictions and the habitual tendencies of ignorance so that they never again continue, and with the stainless noble path as radiant as the sun, he prostrates once before the Buddha.
"Next, pay homage to the Great Canon of the Dharma-Wheel, consisting of the twelve divisions of the honored scriptures:

Namo to the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*; Namo to the *Bodhisattva-svapna Sūtra*; Namo to the *Bodhisattva-ṛddhi-vikurvāṇa Sūtra*; Namo to the *Dharmadhātu-svabhāva Sūtra*; Namo to the *Guhyagarbha Sūtra*; Namo to the *Pratyutpanna Sūtra*. From this point upward, [homage is paid] to the one thousand seven hundred Buddhas, the twelve divisions of the scriptures, and all the worthy and holy ones."
Homage to the *Sūtra of the Sun Transcending Radiance*.
Homage to the *Madhyama-āgama Sūtra on the Origin of Events*.
Homage to the *Sūtra on the Praise of the Prince*.
Homage to the *Sūtra of the Victorious Śyāma*.
Homage to the *Sūtra of the Auspicious Radiance*.
Homage to the Sutra of the Three Vehicles Without Obstruction. Next, pay homage to the great bodhisattvas of the ten directions:
Homage to the Bodhisattva Courageous Wisdom;
homage to the Bodhisattva Delivering from Difficulties;
homage to the Bodhisattva Saving Spirit.
Homage to Bodhisattva Duanadu (Dunāṇa). Homage to Bodhisattva Mīdara.
Next, pay homage to all the worthy and holy ones among the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas: Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Jien Feiteng (Jin-puruṣa-vikrama).

Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Kēbōluo (Kapphina). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Qīnmólì (Candramas). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Yuèjìng (Candraprabha). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Shànzhì (Sumati). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Xiūtúluó (Sudatta). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Shàn fă (Dharmika). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Yìngqiú (Yathārthika). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Jìqiú (Śikhin). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Dàshì (Mahāsthāman). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Xiūxíng bùzhuó (Anadhiṣṭhita-caryā). Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Shě (Pratibhāna). I take refuge in these and all other immeasurable and boundless Pratyekabuddhas.
"Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we now proceed to repentance.
'Disciples! Having briefly completed the repentance for the obstacle of afflictions (*kleśāvaraṇa*), we shall now, in due order, repent for the obstacle of karma (*karmāvaraṇa*')."

Indeed, karma is able to adorn and embellish every realm and every location throughout the world; therefore, one should contemplate seeking liberation from the world. One should know that the various differences in the retributions of the six realms, and the distinctness of their forms and types, are all produced by the power of karma.
Therefore, among the Buddha’s ten powers, the power of karma is most profound, and ordinary people frequently give rise to doubts and delusions regarding it.

Why is this so? We see in the world that those who practice virtue encounter misfortune at every turn, while those who commit evil find their affairs prospering; consequently, they claim that in the world there is no distinction between good and evil.
Those who calculate in this manner are all unable to penetrate deeply into the principles of karma. Why is this so?
For it is said in the Sūtras:
First, karma to be experienced in the present life;..."
The second is retribution in this life;
the third is retribution in a future life.
Regarding karma that yields retribution in the present life: when one performs good or evil deeds in the present, one receives the retribution in the present body.
Karma to be experienced in the present life refers to performing wholesome or unwholesome deeds in this life and receiving their retribution in the next life.

Karma to be experienced in subsequent lives refers to performing wholesome or unwholesome deeds either in immeasurable past lives or in this life, and receiving their retribution either in this life, or in immeasurable future lives.

As for those who previously committed evil yet now appear to experience good fortune, this is because the ripening of their past-life karma—either as immediate retribution (*vipāka*) or subsequent retribution—is maturing; thus, they enjoy these pleasant fruits in the present. How could this have anything to do with performing various evil deeds in the present and receiving a favorable reward?

When a person who practices virtue experiences suffering in the present life, it is because the retributions of evil karma from past lives—whether ripening in this lifetime (*janma-vedanīya*) or in subsequent lifetimes (*aparaparyāya-vedanīya*)—have matured; thus, the power of their current roots of goodness is too weak to dispel it, and they consequently receive this bitter retribution. How does this concern the fact that performing good deeds in the present would result in an evil retribution?
How is this known to be so?
Those in the present world who perform wholesome deeds are praised by others and held in respect by others; therefore, we know that they will necessarily bring forth pleasant fruits in the future.

Since such evil karma exists from the past, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas instruct one to draw near to virtuous conduct and to perform repentance in common with others; for those who understand this well, it serves as a benefit within the attainment of the Way.
Therefore, disciples, today we take refuge with utmost sincerity in the Buddha: Homage to the Buddha Immeasurable Freedom from Defilement in the East;

Homage to the Buddha Tree-Root Flower King in the South; Homage to the Buddha Lotus Sovereign in the West; Homage to the Buddha Vajra Capable of Shattering in the North; Homage to the Buddha Supreme in the Meaning of Siddhānta in the Southeast; Homage to the Buddha Sovereign King of the Golden Ocean in the Southwest; Homage to the Buddha Infinite Dharma Sovereign in the Northwest; Homage to the Buddha Unobstructed Fragrant Elephant King in the Northeast; Homage to the Buddha Banner of Unobstructed Wisdom below; Homage to the Buddha Ambrosia Supreme King above. Thus, [we take refuge] in all the Triple Gem throughout the entirety of the empty realm of the ten directions.

"Disciples! From beginningless time until this very day, you have accumulated evils as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and committed sins that fill the heavens and the earth; yet, in casting off one body and receiving another, you have neither perceived nor known it."

Some commit the grave offenses of the five heinous crimes, bound by deep and turbid afflictions; some create the karma of an icchantika who has severed their roots of goodness; they slander the Buddha’s words and denigrate the Vaipulya sutras; they destroy the Triple Gem and ruin the True Dharma; they do not believe in sin or merit and give rise to the ten non-virtuous actions; they are deluded regarding the truth and turn away from the right path through ignorant confusion; they are unfilial toward their two parents and act with perverse rebellion; they treat their teachers and elders with contempt and lack the conduct of reverence; and they are untrustworthy and unrighteous toward their friends.

Or they may create karma that constitutes fourfold, sixfold, or eightfold obstructions to the Noble Path; karma of violating the five precepts or breaking the eight observances; karma of frequently neglecting or transgressing the five categories and seven groups of offenses; and karma of light and heavy defilements regarding the Upāsaka precepts.

Or, the Bodhisattva precepts may not be pure as prescribed for their practice; the preliminary and concluding expedients may defile the Brahma-conduct; one may neglect the six fast days of the month through the karma of indolence; one may fail to constantly observe the practices during the three long periods of the year; one’s conduct regarding the three thousand dignified manners may be contrary to the Dharma; one may commit subtle offenses regarding the eighty thousand dignified manners; one may fail to follow the true karma of body, precepts, and mind; one may create various karmas of transgression during the eight kings of spring and autumn; and one may engage in the karma of the sixteen kinds of evil non-disciplined conduct.

These are: the karma of lacking compassion for suffering sentient beings; the karma of failing to feel pity; the karma of neither uprooting nor rescuing, and providing no protection; the karma of harboring jealousy and failing to deliver others; the karma of being partial toward enemies and kin; and the karma of indulging in the five desires without weariness or renunciation.

Or, due to livelihoods involving clothing, food, gardens, and ponds, or through the dissolute occupations of worldly life; or, during the prime of youth, by indulging in sensual desires and creating various karmic offenses; or, by dedicating wholesome yet outflowing (*sāsrava*) merit toward the three realms of existence (*trai-dhātuka*), thereby obstructing the karma for transcendence from the world.
Such karmas as these are immeasurable and boundless; today we reveal them before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Noble Assembly, and repent of them all.

"We pray that by virtue of the merit and goodness arising from this confession of our various karmas, including those of the immediate offenses, may our disciples, in birth after birth, extinguish the five heinous crimes and eliminate the state of icchantika."

Should one have committed such light or heavy transgressions, from this day forward until reaching the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), they vow never to commit them again. They shall constantly practice supramundane, pure, and wholesome dharmas, diligently maintaining the conduct of the Vinaya, guarding the Way, and preserving dignified deportment. Like one crossing the ocean who cherishes their life-preserving float, they shall always cultivate the path through the six perfections, the four immeasurables, and the categories of morality, concentration, and wisdom. Thus, they shall further attain increased clarity and swiftly accomplish the Tathāgata’s thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the three kinds of mindfulness, great compassion, constant bliss, wondrous wisdom, and the eightfold self-mastery. Having paid this single prostration, [one should proceed].
The Sutra of the Names of Buddhas, Scroll Two: Next, pay homage to the Great Treasury of the Dharma Wheel consisting of the twelve divisions of the honored sutras.
Homage to the *Sutra of Maitreya’s Ascent to Be Born Above*;
Homage to the *Dharmapada-śāstra* (The Scripture on the Transmission of the Dharma-treasury).
Homage to the *Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra*. Homage to the *Laṅkāvatāra-ārya-sūtra*.
homage to the Subāhu Bodhisattva Sūtra;
Homage to the Buddhas who have spoken the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*,
homage to the Buddhas who have spoken the *Ānāpāna Sūtra*,

and homage to the Buddhas who have spoken the *Daśapratyaya Sūtra*. To all the Buddhas from this point upward, numbering four thousand nine hundred, to the twelve divisions of the scriptures, and to all the worthy ones and sages.

“Homage to the Buddha who spoke the *Parinirvāṇa Sūtra*. Homage to the Buddha who spoke the *Vinayaviniścaya Sūtra*. Homage to the Buddha who spoke the *Maitreya-bodhisattva-tuṣitabhavana-upapatti-darśana Sūtra*. Homage to the Buddha who spoke the *Durbalādhāna Sūtra*. Homage to the *Saṃtati-vimokṣa Sūtra*. Homage to the *Rathavinīta Sūtra*. Homage to the *Sahasrabuddhanāman* and the *Saptati-buddhanāma Sūtra*. Homage to the *Saṃghakṣānti Sūtra*. Homage to the *Chanda Sūtra*. Next, pay homage to the great bodhisattvas of the ten directions.”
homage to the Bodhisattva Who Turns the Non-retrogressive Wheel of Dharma;
homage to the Bodhisattva Who Turns the Wheel of Dharma upon Resolving the Mind.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Subtle Features Adorned with Purity.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Who Deceives No Sentient Being.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Ocean of Immeasurable Merit-Mind.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Constantly Steadfast and Undisturbed Faculties; homage to the Bodhisattva Jewel-Mind.
Next, pay homage to all the worthy sages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas:

Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Arhita; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Bhalita; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Takāru; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Yaśas; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Darśana; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Priyadarśana; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Buddha; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Gandhara; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Bhārya; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Riṣabha. Having paid homage to the Three Jewels, next perform repentance once again.
"I have already repented the obstacle of afflictions and repented the obstacle of karma; I shall now proceed in order to lay bare and repent the obstacle of retribution.
As it is said in the Sūtras:

'When the retribution for karma arrives, there is no place where one may escape it and avoid receiving it—not in the void, nor in the midst of the ocean, nor by entering between mountain rocks; there is no other location where one may evade it.'"
"Only through the power of repentance can these be eliminated. How is this known?

When Śakra Devānām-Indra beheld the five signs of decay, his heart was filled with intense fear; he returned with sincerity to the Triple Gem, whereupon the five signs immediately vanished and he was granted an extension to his celestial lifespan."

As clarified by such scriptural teachings, if a person does not encounter a virtuous friend to guide them on the path, there is no evil they will not commit; consequently, when their life is about to end and they reach its final limit, the horrific manifestations of hell appear before them.
At that time, remorse and fear will arrive together; failing to cultivate goodness in advance, one repents only when facing the ultimate limit.

What can be done then? Calamities and misfortunes have long been prepared in another place; one must go alone into the distant hells. Upon reaching one's destination, one enters the fiery cauldrons, where body and mind are shattered and the spirit suffers agony. At such a time, how could one possibly obtain even a single prostration or a single confession?

“Sentient beings, do not rely on your own youth, wealth, or power, nor indulge in indolence, laziness, and self-indulgence. When the suffering of death arrives, it makes no distinction between old and young; whether one is poor or rich, noble or lowly, all are utterly extinguished. It comes suddenly and unexpectedly, such that people do not even realize they have lost [their lives].”
Human life is impermanent, like the morning dew; though the outgoing breath may enter, the incoming breath cannot be guaranteed. Why, then, do you not repent?
Moreover, once the five celestial messengers have arrived and the executioner of impermanence has suddenly come, even those in the prime of youth and vigor cannot escape.
At that time, what concern have the magnificent halls and deep chambers for human affairs? How could the high carriages and great horses follow one of their own accord?
Wives, children, and kinsmen are no longer my kin; the ornaments of the seven treasures become merely the playthings of others.
Speaking from this perspective, all worldly retributions are but illusory transformations.
Though the heavens may be pleasant, they ultimately revert to decay; when life is exhausted and the soul departs, one falls into the three miserable realms.
Therefore, the Buddha said to Subhadra:

"The Dharma-master Udraka Rāmaputra possessed sharp faculties and great intelligence; he was able to subdue his afflictions and reach the station of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Yet, at the end of his life, he returned to take birth as a flying fox among the animals—how much more so for others?"

Thus one should know that from the time before attaining the fruits of sainthood (āryaphala) and prior to that, one must undergo the cycle of rebirth and experience all the evil destinies; if one is not careful, one may suddenly find oneself personally beset by such matters one day—how could one then fail to regret it?

Even as it is now a minor suffering when one is accused of a crime before the various government offices— where one is terrified in spirit and one's kinsmen are struck with fear, seeking salvation by every possible means—
the manifold sufferings of the hells cannot be compared to these, being hundreds of thousands of millions of times greater beyond all analogy.
"Since time immemorial, the sins of you all have been as vast as Mount Sumeru; how can you hear this and remain so composed, neither fearing, nor trembling, nor being alarmed?
To cause these spirits to once again suffer such agony is truly a matter for lamentation."
Therefore, we disciples direct this single sincerity toward taking refuge in the Buddha:

Homage to the Buddha Tamer of Beings in the East. Homage to the Buddha Vajragarbha in the South. Homage to the Buddha Ascending the Dharma-realm in the West. Homage to the Buddha Boundless Eye in the North. Homage to the Buddha Sorrowless Virtue in the Southeast. Homage to the Buddha Destroyer of All Faculties in the Southwest. Homage to the Buddha Valiant Subduer in the Northwest. Homage to the Buddha Great Power Radiance in the Northeast. Homage to the Buddha Path of Joy in the Nadir. Homage to the Buddha Fragrant Supreme King in the Zenith. We disciples!

From beginningless time until this day, there have been all manner of karmic obstacles; however, among those that are most grave, the foremost is none other than the Avīci Hell, as clarified in the sūtras. Now, I shall briefly describe its characteristics.

This hell is surrounded on all sides by seven layers of iron walls and further covered above and below by seven layers of iron nets. There are seven layers of sword-forests and immeasurable fierce fires, spanning eighty-four thousand yojanas in length and breadth.

The bodies of the offenders fill the entire space; through the causal conditions of their sinful karma, they do not obstruct one another. The upper fires penetrate downward and the lower fires penetrate upward; east, west, south, and north are completely permeated and intermingled. Just as when fish are placed in a cauldron until their fat and grease are entirely consumed, so too is the suffering of sin within this place.

"At the four gates of that city are four great copper dogs; their bodies are four thousand yojanas in length and breadth, their fangs are like sharp plowshares, and their eyes flash like lightning. Furthermore, there are immeasurable iron-beaked birds that flap their wings and soar upward to devour the flesh of the sinners."
The ox-headed hell-wardens have forms like rākṣasas and possess nine tails, whose ends resemble iron forks;
they further have eight heads, each topped with eighteen horns;

they have sixty-four eyes, from every single eye of which iron balls burst forth to scorch the flesh of the sinners; and whenever they roar in their singular malice and rage, their voices sound like thunderclaps.

Furthermore, immeasurable natural wheels of blades descend from the sky, entering through the crowns of the offenders' heads and exiting through their feet; thus, the pain of these offenders penetrates to the very marrow of their bones, and the suffering pierces their livers and hearts.
Thus, for immeasurable years, they sought life but could not find it, and sought death but could not find it; for such retributions as these, we today all prostrate ourselves in shame and repentance.
"I repent for the retribution of having one's head and body severed upon the mountains of blades and trees of swords in the remaining hells;

I repent for the retribution of being burned and boiled in the cauldrons of boiling water and the furnaces of burning coals; I repent for the retribution of being scorched and ignited upon the iron beds and copper pillars;
I repent for the retribution of being split, crushed, and ground by the wheels of blades and the chariots of fire; I repent for the retribution of having my tongue pulled out."

I repent for the retribution of suffering and pain in the Plow-field Hell; I repent for the retribution of the five internal organs being consumed and rotted by swallowing iron balls and having molten copper poured into the mouth in the Hell of Iron Balls and Molten Copper;
I repent for the retribution of bones and flesh being ground to dust in the Hell of Iron Mortars and Iron Mills;
I repent for the retribution of limbs and joints being severed and separated in the Black Rope and Iron-Copper Hells.
I repent for the retribution of suffering and distress in the Hell of the Boiling Ash-River and Excrement;

I repent for the retribution of having skin split and being nakedly frozen in the Hell of Salt Water and Cold Ice; I repent for the retribution of mutual slaughter and injury in the Hell of Tigers, Wolves, Hawks, and Dogs;
and I repent for the retribution of mutual seizing, stabbing, and piercing in the Hell of Fire Pits and Iron Spikes.
I repent for the retribution of being roasted and broiled in the Hell of the Fire Pit; I repent for the retribution of having one's body shattered in the Hell of Mutual Calumny and Quarreling;
I repent for the retribution of being dismembered in the Hell of the Black-Eared Mass-Press;
I repent for the retribution of being hacked and minced in the Hell of the Dark Flesh Mountain; [and I repent for the retribution of] the Hell of Being Sawn Apart and Nailed to the Body.
Repentance for the retribution of being severed and cut; repentance for the retribution of being slaughtered and dismembered while suspended upside down by iron clubs in hell;
repentance for the retribution of the distress and anguish in the Reviving and Screaming Hells;
and repentance for the retribution of wandering in the perpetual darkness between the Great and Small Iron Ring Mountains, unable to perceive the three luminaries.

The Abbāpā hell, the Ababa hell, the Aṭaṭa hell, and the Alala hell—thus there are all the eight cold and eight hot hells. Within each individual hell, there are further eighty-four thousand subsidiary "partitioned" hells as its retinue. Within these, the sufferings of the transgressions—such as being roasted, scorched, tormented, flayed, having flesh torn away, bones scraped, marrow beaten out, entrails pulled, and being struck with staves—are immeasurable; they are such that they cannot be heard and cannot be described.
Those who are here within this place today may be our parents from beginningless births or all our kinsmen; after we pass away, we too may fall into such a hell as this.”

Today, with a purified heart and utmost sincerity, I prostrate myself with my head to the ground before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas of the great earth, entreating their compassion to repent; may all these karmic obstacles of retribution now be utterly extinguished.

"May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession of the retributions of the hells and other realms, immediately shatter the iron city of Avīci; may all pure lands be such that even the names of evil paths do not exist; may all other instruments of suffering in the hells be transformed into conditions for joy; may the mountain of knives and trees of swords become forests of jewels; may the boiling cauldrons and furnace coals transform into the spontaneous birth of lotus flowers; may the ox-headed hell-wardens remove their feverish cruelty and give rise to compassion, harboring no ill will; may the sentient beings in the hells be freed from the fruits of suffering and never again create the causes for it, receiving peace and happiness like those in the Third Dhyāna; and may they simultaneously resolve upon the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment and perform one prostration."
"Next, pay homage to the Great Canon of the Dharma-Wheel, consisting of the twelve divisions of the honored scriptures:

'Namo to the *Aṣṭanāgarājaparipṛcchā-mantra-sūtra*; Namo to the *Sahyu-sūtra*; Namo to the *Kumārajīva-avadāna-sūtra*; Namo to the *Śāli-stamba-sūtra*. From this point upward, [homage is paid] to the five thousand four hundred Buddhas, the twelve divisions of the scriptures, and all worthy sages."
Homage to the *Sūtra on the Evil Verses Spoken by King Avalokita*; homage to the *Śukasūtra*;
Homage to the Buddha who spoke the Sūtra on the Four Vows;
homage to the Buddha who spoke the Sūtra on the Six-Syllable Mantra King;
homage to the Buddha who spoke the Kāśyapa Sūtra.

Homage to the *Sūtra on the Wild Chicken*.

Homage to the Bodhisattva Sea-Virtue Jewel-Adorned Pure-Mind.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Great Adornment-Purity.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Great Marks.
Homage to the Bodhisattva King of Joy;
homage to the Bodhisattva Firm Power;
homage to the Bodhisattva Firm Resolve.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreyarājakumāra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāmaṅgalyakumāra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Brahmaghoṣakumāra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Prince of Dharma Wondrous Color.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Prince of Dharma Sandalwood Forest.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Prince of Dharma Lion’s Roar Sound.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjusvara Dharmarāja.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Varṇarūpendriya Dharmarāja.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Citravyūha Dharmarāja.

homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mūrdhaja Dharma-Prince. Next, pay homage to all the worthy and holy ones of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

“Homage to the Pratyekabuddha Śruta; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Jñānakāya; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Vaiśālī; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Kośala; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Posadharāja; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Viṣamukta-viśuddhacitta; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Bhūtavimala; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Puṇyavanta; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Kṛṣṇa; homage to the Pratyekabuddha Kevalakṛṣṇa. Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, one next performs repentance.
"Having finished repenting for the retribution of the hells, we shall now, in turn, repent for the retribution of the three evil realms.
In the sutras, the Buddha said:
'Those who have many desires suffer much affliction because they seek many gains;'"
"One who knows contentment finds joy even when lying upon the ground;
one who lacks contentment finds no satisfaction even while dwelling in heaven.

Yet worldly people, when suddenly faced with urgent calamity, are able to give away their wealth regardless of its amount, without realizing that this body stands upon the edge of a deep pit leading to the three miserable realms, and that with a single breath not returned, it must fall.
Suppose there is a spiritual friend who, wishing to cultivate merit and virtue, urges one to prepare the provisions for wholesome dharmas in the future;
yet, clinging to this stingy mind, one refuses to act accordingly. Such a person is utterly deluded and foolish!
Why is this so? In the sutras, the Buddha said:

"At birth, one does not bring a single coin; at death, one does not take a single coin with one. One exhausts the body through accumulation and suffers distress for its sake, yet it benefits oneself not at all but serves only as the property of others. Having no goodness to rely upon and no attainment to depend on, when life ends, one falls into the various evil realms."
"Therefore, disciples! Today, with heads bowed in prostration and with utmost sincerity, we take refuge in the Buddha:

Homage to the Buddha Great Radiance in the East; Homage to the Buddha Dwelling in Space in the South; Homage to the Buddha Vajra-Step in the West; Homage to the Buddha Boundless Power in the North; Homage to the Buddha Boundless King in the Southeast; Homage to the Buddha Destroyer of All Enemies in the Southwest; Homage to the Buddha Golden Light Sound in the Northwest; Homage to the Buddha Stainless Light in the Northeast; Homage to the Buddha Lion’s Play in the Nadir; Homage to the Buddha Moon Banner King in the Zenith."
“In this way, [I take refuge in] all the Three Jewels throughout the entirety of the space of the ten directions.

Disciple! Today, I further repent for the retribution of my sins in the realm of animals where there is no discernment; I repent for the retribution of my sins in the realm of animals where I bore heavy burdens, were harnessed and led, and repaid past debts to others; I repent for the retribution of my sins in the realm of animals where I lacked autonomy and was hacked, pierced, butchered, and carved by others; I repent for the retribution of my sins as an animal with no feet, two feet, four feet, or many feet; and I repent for the retribution of my sins in the realm of animals where the various hairs, feathers, scales, and shells of my body were pecked and eaten by tiny insects.”
Thus, within the realm of animals there are immeasurable retributions for transgressions; today, with utmost sincerity, we repent them all in their entirety.

Next, we further repent the retribution of long-term hunger within the realm of hungry ghosts; we repent the retribution of hungry ghosts who for thousands of millions of years have never heard the name of water or drink; we repent the retribution of hungry ghosts who devour pus, blood, excrement, and filth; we repent the retribution of hungry ghosts whose every limb and joint bursts into flames whenever they move their bodies; and we repent the retribution of hungry ghosts who have vast bellies and tiny throats.
Thus, regarding the immeasurable retributions of suffering within the realm of hungry ghosts, I now prostrate my head in total repentance.

Furthermore, regarding the retributions for flattery, deceit, and false claims within the realms of all spirits, ghosts, and asuras, I repent. Regarding the retributions for carrying sand and bearing stones to fill rivers and block oceans within the realm of spirits and ghosts, I repent. Regarding the retributions for being born as spirits, ghosts, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and various other malevolent spirits who devour flesh and blood raw and endure such loathsome forms, I repent.

Thus, all the immeasurable and boundless retributions for sins within the realm of ghosts and spirits, I today prostrate myself before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas of the great earth, seeking their compassion to repent so that they may all be extinguished.

"May we, the disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession of the retribution of animal births and so forth, extinguish the defilement of ignorance in life after life, recognize our own karmic conditions, and with the clear illumination of wisdom, sever the body of the evil realms."

By the merit produced through this repentance for the retribution of hungry ghosts and others, may we, in birth after birth and life after life, forever be free from the suffering of stinginess, greed, hunger, and thirst, and always partake of the nectar-like flavor of liberation.

By virtue of the merit generated through this repentance for the retributions of ghosts, spirits, and asuras, may I be upright and sincere in every birth and lifetime, free from flattery, depart from the causes of wrong livelihood, eliminate the fruits of ugliness, and bring benefit and welfare to humans and devas.

"May we, the disciples, from this day forth until our certain arrival at the site of enlightenment, never again receive retribution in the four evil realms; except that, for the sake of sentient beings out of great compassion, we shall remain there through the power of our vows without weariness."

Having performed one prostration, I respectfully transcribe this sixth fascicle of the *Sūtra of the Names of Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha*, totaling two hundred and eighty-eight fascicles of the *Mahābuddhanāmasūtra*. I pray that the city god (Chenghuang) may enjoy peace and stability, the common people may be healthy and tranquil, and that the Prefectural Governor, Minister Cao, may enjoy eternal longevity, succeed to his lineage for generations, and that his entire household and kin may always abide in auspiciousness and joy.
Recorded on the fifteenth day of the fifth month in the year of Gengchen, during the Zhenming era of the Great Liang dynasty.

Homage to the Bodhisattva Akṣayacchanda. Next, pay homage to all the worthy and holy ones among the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas:

Homage to the Venerable Udāyin. Homage to the Venerable Cūḍapanthaka. Homage to the Venerable Ghaṭīkāra. Homage to the Venerable Trapusa. Homage to the Venerable Aśvajit. Homage to the Venerable Bhadrika. Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, one next performs repentance.
"There are three kinds of craving, namely: craving for sense-desires, craving for form, and craving for the formless.

Desire is called negligence; through the conditions of negligence, craving-contact arises. Through the conditions of contact, the perception of pleasure arises. Sentient beings delight in and become attached to such phenomena as these; their desirous minds are incited as if being consumed by fire. Due to the causes and conditions of desire, they take pleasure in committing the ten unwholesome actions and abandon the ten wholesome ones.
By these causes and conditions, they fall into the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts, or are born among the impoverished yakṣas.

Due to the causes and conditions of desire, they undergo the bodies of the five aggregates within saṃsāra, experiencing all manner of sufferings; yet, though they endure such suffering, they do not give rise to fear, their minds lack shame and remorse, and they take no pleasure in cultivating goodness. Thus, amidst the cycle of transmigration, it is difficult for them to obtain a human body.

Even if one obtains a human body, due to the causes and conditions of desire, one’s body and speech become impure, and one commits immeasurable grave evil karmas, even up to the five deeds of immediate retribution; by these causes and conditions, one further undergoes great and heavy suffering within the three evil realms of cyclic existence.

All suffering experienced arises from the accumulation of causes and conditions rooted in the mind of desire; it is like a dung-eating pig that, once bound, falls into the three evil realms and undergoes all manner of afflictions and distress.
"Therefore, in order to sever craving, the Tathāgata proclaims the True Dharma and censures the phenomena of desire.

If there are sentient beings who, having heard such censure of desire, are able to contemplate all desires as they truly are—impure like the fruit of a poisonous tree, like a great mass of fire, like a jar full of poison, like a jar full of excrement, like a sharp blade, like a *caṇḍāla* thief or *gaṭhina*, like a red-hot iron ball, like a great shower of hail, like the fierce *vilambha* wind, like a venomous serpent, like a treacherous wild marsh, like a *rākṣasa* island, like *bhadragauḍa*, like various heaps of refuse, and like a *śītavana* cemetery."

Thus perceiving the faults and afflictions of desire, he conceived a great dread toward sensual matters, his body trembling violently. He came to love the Dharma, delight in the Dharma, and study the Dharma; he shaved off his hair and beard and donned the dharma-robes. Seeking the True Dharma and seeking mastery over the Dharma, he gave rise to a pure mind within the True Dharma and practiced the deliverance of the Dharma-path.

One who delights in this manner will attain right mindfulness at the time of death; because they mindfully contemplate the Dharma, because they delight in the flavor of the Dharma, and because they mindfully contemplate the karmic fruition of the Dharma, they shall see the Buddhas of the ten directions amidst great assemblies proclaiming the essentials of the Dharma to teach and transform sentient beings.
Having heard the Dharma, they attain a heart of joy; because their hearts are joyful, they repeatedly behold the form-bodies (*rūpakāya*) of the Buddhas.

After this person dies, they leave behind the three evil realms and are born in a Buddha-field, always dwelling and associating with virtuous people. They are able to practice generosity, patience, and diligence; they delight in meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), cultivate the five supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), and take pleasure in the path to Nirvāṇa. With great compassion, they teach and transform sentient beings, and are able to attain the merit-body adorned with the ornaments of all Buddhas.
All past afflictions and habitual tendencies are completely extinguished.

Those sentient beings attain such adornment of body and mind; it is like a fragrant casket containing various garments: the clothes are all fragrant, yet the fragrance and flowers do not lose their weight nor diminish their color.
“Kauṇḍinya! Within the desire realm there are eight great hells; each of these hells has sixteen subsidiary hells on its four sides as its retinue, surrounding it on all sides.”
first, the hell of alternating death and life;
seventh is the Great Reviving Hell;

"If there are sentient beings who, having created various evil karmas through their own body, speech, and mind, are consequently born in that great hell, where they undergo various sufferings for immeasurable kalpas, passing from one hell to another, experiencing the most extreme of pains that are utterly unbearable."
Their bodies are constantly ablaze as they eat glowing iron balls and drink molten copper; because their evil karma has not yet been exhausted, they do not die in this manner.

Among the animals, there are some whose bodies are like motes of dust drifting in a window, while others have bodies ten thousand *yojanas* in length. Some beings have a lifespan of but a moment, while others have a lifespan of an entire eon. Due to their evil karma, they are born therein; they do not know wholesome dharmas and possess no wisdom. Constantly practicing unwholesome deeds in the darkness of ignorance, they perpetually suffer from hunger and thirst within these perilous and evil paths. They are beaten, ridden, and burdened until they are exhausted; their necks are pierced and their backs broken, as mosquitoes, gadflies, and venomous insects vied with one another to bite and devour them.

"Among the hungry ghosts (preta), some are one foot tall; some are the size of humans; some are as large as a thousand *yojana*; and some have bodies like the Snow Mountains. They are naked with no clothing, their hair entangling them; they are black, emaciated, and gaunt, possessing only skin wrapping their bones, while flesh and blood are entirely absent. Their bodies are coarse and rough like withered trees; they suffer constantly from hunger and thirst, with fire burning within their mouths and flames issuing forth from them. Their minds are perpetually filled with anger and resentment, devoid of compassion; they are tormented by heat and panic, seeking coolness but finding none. As they contemplate this suffering, further suffering arises; through suffering they produce suffering, thereby creating the causes for more suffering, so that in future lives they shall again undergo the retribution of suffering."

"Thus, the sufferings of these three evil realms are immeasurable and boundless; today, with utmost sincerity, I repent for them all. Within the emptiness of the *dharmatā*, there is neither bondage nor liberation; sinful karma arises in various ways according to the mind. If one can contemplate that the mind is without action or reception, all seeds of karma will be utterly extinguished."
Having completed the repentance, take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem: Homage to the Buddha Destroyer of All Afflictions. Homage to the Buddha Sovereign of Wondrous Sound.
