"Homage to the Venerable Śāriputra; homage to the Venerable Maudgalyāyana; homage to the Venerable Aniruddha; homage to the Venerable Kanakavatsa; homage to the Venerable Madhyāntika; homage to the Venerable Śāṇakavāsin; homage to the Venerable Upagupta; homage to the Venerable Miśraka. Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we shall next perform repentance."
"Next is the repentance for the karma of theft.

'If an object belongs to another and is protected by another, one must not take even a single blade of grass or a single leaf from among those objects without it being given; how much less so should one commit theft?'"

"However, because sentient beings see only the benefits of the present, they take what is not given through various unrighteous means, thereby causing themselves to suffer these calamities and burdens in the future.
For this reason, the Sūtra says:
'The sin of robbery can cause sentient beings to fall into the hells or as hungry ghosts to undergo suffering.'"
If they are born among animals, they take on the forms of oxen, horses, donkeys, mules, camels, and the like, repaying their past debts with the physical strength, blood, and flesh of their bodies.

If they are born among humans, they become servants or slaves to others; their clothing does not cover their bodies and their food does not sustain their lives, suffering from poverty and hardship until their basic human dignity is nearly extinguished.
"Since there are such bitter retributions for robbery and theft, therefore, disciples! Today, having arrived here, we prostrate ourselves and take refuge in the Buddha.

Homage to the Buddha Destroyer of All Afflictions in the East. Homage to the Buddha Sovereign of Wondrous Sound in the South. Homage to the Buddha Great Cloud Radiance in the West. Homage to the Buddha Cloud Sovereign King in the North. Homage to the Buddha Adorned with Unconditioned [Vows] in the Southeast. Homage to the Buddha Transcending All Mara Realms in the Southwest. Homage to the Buddha Seeing No Fear in the Northwest. Homage to the Buddha Adorned with All Virtues in the Northeast. Homage to the Buddha Lotus Treasury Radiance in the Upper Direction. Homage to the Buddha Sovereign King of Wondrous Abiding in the Lower Direction. Thus, [we take refuge in] all the Triple Gems throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space in the ten directions."

"Disciple! From beginningless time until this very day, you may have stolen others' wealth and treasures, seizing them by force with weapons; or, relying on your own person, you may have coerced and taken [property]; or, relying on official authority, or feigning power, you may have unjustly oppressed the virtuous with high stocks and heavy shackles; or, having swallowed bribes and accepted illicit goods, you may have perverted the upright into the crooked. Due to these causes and conditions, your body has been ensnared in the net of the law."

Or they may govern with depravity, misappropriating the wealth and property of others; they may encroach upon public funds for private gain or use private assets for public benefit; they may harm others to profit themselves or harm themselves to profit others; they may seize from others to enrich themselves, while their mouths offer words of generosity but their hearts harbor stinginess.
Whether by secretly evading taxes and assessments, stealing through customs duties, concealing public grain levies, or hiding corvée laborers—
such transgressions as these, I now repent of them all.

"Whether it be taking what belongs to the Buddha or the Sangha without it being given; or objects belonging to scriptures and images, or objects for the repair of stupas and temples; or objects intended for the support of the resident (sthavira) Sangha, or objects designated for the universal (cāturmahārājakāyika) Sangha; or stealing and misusing them, or failing to return them by relying on one's power; or lending them to others oneself, or exchanging and lending them while forgetting; or confusing and using the property of the Triple Gem indiscriminately; or using the community’s goods—such as grain, firewood, salt, soybeans, sauce, vinegar, vegetables, fruits, money, silk, bamboo, wood, brocade, banners, canopies, incense, flowers, oil, and candles—according to one's own whims and desires, whether using them oneself or giving them to others; or plucking flowers and fruit from the Buddha, or using the items of the Sangha’s garlands; thus privately profiting oneself from the wealth of the Triple Gem."
Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless; today, with shame and remorse, I confess them all.

Furthermore, from beginningless time until this day, whether acting as friends, associates, teachers, monks, fellow students, parents, brothers, or other six types of kinsmen, living together and dwelling in the same place, we have deceived one another regarding the hundreds of necessities of life;

or, as neighbors and close acquaintances, we have shifted fences and expanded walls to encroach upon others' lands and houses, altered boundary markers and changed signs to seize their gardens and fields, or used public affairs as a pretext for private gain to usurp people's shops and dwellings, as well as their rural estates.
All such offenses as these, I now fully repent.

Furthermore, since beginningless time, I have besieged cities, destroyed towns, burned villages, and demolished stockades; I have stolen and sold free citizens, and enticed away the servants of others.

Or again, they may unjustly oppress innocent people, causing their bodies to perish by the edge of the blade and their persons to be bound in fetters; their family estates are ruined and scattered, and their kin are separated by birth, divided across distant lands with life and death cut off from one another.
Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless; I now come before you all to repent them completely.

Furthermore, from time immemorial until this day, whether in commerce, trade, or business at market stalls, I have used light scales and small measures to reduce weights and dimensions, stealing fractions of a grain and deceiving others regarding the *gui* and *he*. I have exchanged coarse goods for the fine and short items for the long, employing hundreds of clever deceptions in hopes of gaining even a hair’s breadth of profit.
All such offenses as these, I now fully repent.

Furthermore, from beginningless time until this day, I have breached walls and leaped over fences, waylaid travelers on the roads, resisted the repayment of debts and interests, betrayed trusts, and deceived others face-to-face with my mind and mouth; or, by unrighteous means, I have plundered and seized the property of ghosts, spirits, birds, beasts, and all four classes of living beings; or, feigning divination and physiognomy, I have taken the wealth and treasures of others; and so forth, even seeking profit through profit, pursuing evil gains and excessive desires without satiety or contentment.

Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless, beyond the power of words to fully describe. Today, we come before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Noble Assembly to confess them all. "We pray that by the merit arising from this confession of the sins of robbery and theft, our disciples, in birth after birth and life after life, may obtain wish-fulfilling jewels; may the seven treasures, exquisite garments, superior bedding, the nectar of a hundred flavors, and various medicinal decoctions rain down constantly; and may whatever is required according to our wishes arrive immediately upon thought."
All sentient beings are free from thoughts of theft or plunder; all are able to have few desires and know contentment.

They do not indulge in nor are they stained by worldly things, always delighting in giving. They practice the path of urgent rescue, regarding their heads, eyes, marrow, and brains as they would spit or snot, dedicating these acts toward the fulfillment of the *dānapāramitā*.
Having finished the confession and made the vow, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
